**Explanation of the words:**

*Yunazzilu al-malā'ikata bi-l-rūḥ* (He sends down the angels with the Spirit): with the revelation (*wahy*) by which the spirits are given life. What is meant by "the angels" is Jibrīl (Gabriel).

*Khalaqa al-insāna min nuṭfah* (He created man from a drop): a drop of semen.

*Dif' wa manāfi'* (warmth and benefits): that by which you keep warm, and benefits such as honey, milk, meat and riding.

*Ḥīna turīḥūn* (when you bring them back): when you bring them back from their pens.

*Wa ḥīna tasraḥūn* (and when you lead them out): and when you drive them out of their pens to their pastures, that is, the places where they graze.

*Illā bi-shiqq al-anfus* (except with great hardship): except with exertion of the self and great difficulty.

**The meaning of the verses:**

The polytheists in Mecca hastened the punishment and demanded it more than once, so God Most High revealed His words: ﴿The command of God has come﴾, meaning, with your punishment, O you who hasten it. It has drawn near and approached you. Al-Naḍr ibn al-Ḥārith, who said: ﴿O God, if this is indeed the truth from You, then rain down upon us stones from the sky, or bring us a painful punishment﴾ [al-Anfāl: 32], was struck after a few years and was killed at Badr, patiently, and then to Hell. The punishment of the Day of Resurrection for those who hasten it has drawn near in its time. For this reason it is expressed in the past tense, to affirm its certain occurrence and the nearness of its arrival, so there is no sense in hastening it. Therefore God said: ﴿So do not seek to hasten it﴾. His words ﴿Glorified is He and exalted above what they associate﴾ mean: He is far above and sanctified beyond what they associate with Him of false deities, since there is no true god except Him.

His words ﴿He sends down the angels with the Spirit by His command﴾ mean: by His will and permission ﴿upon whom He wills of His servants﴾, that is, Jibrīl (peace be upon him) brings the revelation down upon whomever of His servants He wills, and that is Muḥammad (ﷺ). His words ﴿that warn that there is no god but Me, so fear Me﴾ mean: warn, that is, frighten the polytheists about the consequence of their shirk (association of partners with God), for their shirk is false and will bring upon them a punishment they cannot bear, because there is no god but God, and all deities besides Him are false. So fear God by abandoning shirk and sins, or else you will be exposed to the painful punishment. In these two verses there is an affirmation of revelation and prophethood for the Prophet (ﷺ), and also an affirmation of tawḥīd (affirmation of God's oneness).

He who created the heavens and the earth by His power and knowledge alone, with no one to assist or help Him, deserves to be worshipped, not those dead deities that do not hear, see or speak. ﴿Exalted is He above what they associate﴾ means: He is far above and sanctified beyond the idols and images they associate with Him.

His words ﴿He created man from a drop﴾ mean: from the weakest and most contemptible thing, a drop of semen. He created him in three darknesses and brought him out from his mother's womb knowing nothing, until, when He raised him and he became a man, he became a disputer against God, contending and obstinate, saying: "Who will give life to bones when they are decayed?"

His words ﴿And the livestock He created for you; in them is warmth and benefits, and from them you eat﴾: these are manifestations of divine power, knowledge, wisdom and mercy, which necessitate worshipping Him and abandoning the worship of anything other than Him.

The livestock, namely camels, cattle and sheep, were created by God for the children of Adam and for no one else. They have warmth in them, for people make clothing, rugs and coverings from the wool of sheep and the hair of camels. They have benefits in them, such as milk, butter, ghee, cheese and offspring, for they bear young every year and people benefit from their young. From them they eat various kinds of meat. The One who bestows these blessings is the only one worthy of worship, not any other of His creatures.

His words ﴿And for you in them is beauty﴾ mean: a good and pleasant sight when you bring them back in the evening from pasture to their pens, ﴿and when you lead them out﴾, that is, you drive them out in the morning from their pens to their pastures. This is a spiritual pleasure in the delight of the sight.

His words ﴿And they carry your loads to a land you could not reach except with great hardship﴾ mean: except with exertion of the self and great difficulty. Camels in the desert are like ships at sea, carrying loads from one land to another, and the distance may be so great that a person cannot reach it except with great hardship and by exerting effort and strength. Were it not for camels, the "ships of the desert", horses, mules and donkeys are similar in carrying loads.

So the Creator of these livestock is your Lord; there is no god but Him, so worship Him and do not associate anything with Him. His words ﴿Indeed your Lord﴾ mean: your Creator, your Provider, your Nurturer, and your true God, for whom you have no god other than Him, is truly ﴿Kind, Merciful﴾. The manifestations of His mercy and kindness are evident throughout human life, for were it not for God's gentleness and mercy toward man, he would not have lived a single hour in this worldly life. So to God belongs all praise, and to Him belongs all favour.

From the guidance of these verses:

1. The Day of Resurrection is near, so there is no sense in hastening it, for it is coming without doubt, and everything that is coming is near.

2. Revelation is called "the Spirit" because it gives life to hearts, just as bodies are given life by spirits.

3. An affirmation of tawḥīd, prophethood and the Final Resurrection through mention of the manifestations of divine power, knowledge, wisdom, kindness and mercy.

**Explanation of the Words:**

*"And He creates what you do not know"*: from among the rest of the animals, and among them cars, airplanes and trains.

*"And upon Allah is the direction of the way"*: that is, by His grace and favor, He made clear the straight path, which is Islam.

*"And of it is one that deviates"*: that is, one that swerves from the straight course, which includes all the other creeds, such as Judaism and Christianity.

*"And from it is a tree"*: that is, and by means of it trees grow. Here it refers generally to all plants.

*"In which you pasture"*: you graze your livestock.

*"Subservient by His command"*: that is, by His permission and power.

*"And what He has created for you on earth"*: that is, what He has created for you on earth of animals and various plants.

**The Meaning of the Verses:**

The noble context continues to establish *tawhid* (the oneness of God) by mentioning the manifestations of Allah's power, knowledge, wisdom and mercy. He, the Exalted, said: ﴿And horses, mules and donkeys﴾, that is, He created them, and He is the Creator of all things, for their riding them, when He said: ﴿that you may ride them, and as an adornment﴾, that is, so that they may be an adornment for you in your life. His words ﴿and He creates what you do not know﴾ mean: among created things that are ridden and not ridden, there are wondrous creations. Among the ridden are these vehicles of various kinds, airplanes, and trains, both fast and slow. All of this is His bounty and favor upon His servants. Is it fitting for them to disbelieve in Him and not give Him thanks? Is it fitting for them to associate others with Him in worship?

His words ﴿And upon Allah is the direction of the way﴾: among His bounty and favor, which obligates thanks and worship of Him alone and not another, is that He has made clear the straight way that leads to His pleasure, which is Islam. In contrast, all religions other than Islam, such as Judaism, Christianity, Zoroastrianism and others, are crooked paths that deviate from justice and rectitude. Those who follow them are astray, not guided to perfection or to happiness. This is the meaning of the Exalted's words ﴿And upon Allah is the direction of the way﴾. And His words ﴿And if He willed, He would have guided you all﴾ mean: if the guidance of all people were the object of His will, He would have guided them all, because of His perfect power and knowledge. However, His wisdom did not require the guidance of all people; He guides those who desire guidance and leaves astray those who desire error.

Among the manifestations of His lordship, which necessitate His divinity (that is, His being worshipped), is what comes in the following verses [10, 11, 12, 13, 14, 15]. The Exalted said: ﴿It is He who sent down water from the sky; from it you have drink﴾, which you drink and by which you purify yourselves. ﴿And from it﴾, that is, from the water that He sent down from the sky, comes ﴿a tree﴾, and by "tree" is meant here all plants, whose existence depends on water. His words ﴿in which you pasture﴾ mean: in that vegetation you graze your livestock. One says *sāma al-māshiyah*, meaning he drove the livestock to pasture so that they graze, and *sāmat al-māshiyah*, meaning the livestock grazed on their own. His words, the Exalted: ﴿He causes to grow for you thereby﴾, that is, by what He sent down from the sky of water, ﴿crops, olives, date palms, grapes, and of all fruits﴾, such as fruits and vegetables of various kinds, since all of these depend on water. His words ﴿Indeed in that﴾, that is, in the aforementioned sending down of water and the abundant benefits obtained by it, ﴿is a sign﴾, that is, a clear indication of the existence, power, knowledge, wisdom and mercy of Allah, which necessitates worshipping Him and abandoning the worship of other than Him.

But it is ﴿for a people who give thought﴾, who thus take admonition. As for those who are like beasts and do not reflect on anything, they find no sign, nor even a semblance of a sign, in the entire universe in which they walk about.

His words, the Exalted: ﴿And He subjected for you the night and the day﴾. The night is for stillness and rest, and the day is for work in seeking provision. Their subjection means their continued existence, never separating until Allah permits their end. His words ﴿and the sun and the moon﴾, that is, He subjected them in this way for benefiting from the light and heat of the sun, and the light of the moon for knowing the number of years and for calculation. His words ﴿and the stars are subjected by His command﴾ are likewise. Among the benefits of the stars is being guided by them in the darkness of land and sea, and their being an ornament and beauty for the sky, which is the ceiling of this our abode. His words ﴿Indeed in that﴾, that is, the aforementioned subjection of the night, day, sun, moon and stars, ﴿are signs﴾, many, by which one may be guided to the Creator, to the obligation of worshipping Him, and to His oneness in these. But it is ﴿for a people who reason﴾, that is, those who employ the capacity of their minds to understand things and grasp their secrets and realities. As for those who are like beasts and the insane, who do not reflect, do not reason, and do not understand, they have not a single sign in the whole universe by which to be guided to their Lord, His mercy toward them, and the obligation of thanking Him.

His words, the Exalted: ﴿And what He has created for you on earth﴾, that is, what He has created for you on earth of humans, animals and plants, ﴿of varied colors﴾, and of varied properties, forms, benefits and effects. ﴿Indeed in that﴾ wondrous creation ﴿is a sign﴾, that is, a clear proof of the existence of the Creator, Mighty and Majestic, and the obligation to worship Him and abandon the worship of other than Him. But it is ﴿for a people who remember﴾, who take admonition, and so turn their attention to their Lord, worshipping Him alone by obeying His command and avoiding His prohibition, and thereby they are perfected and attain happiness in both lives.

**Explanation of the words:**

*Ḥilya talbasūnahā* (ornament you wear): it is pearls and coral.

*Mawākhir fīhi* (ploughing through it): that is, cutting through it as it runs, advancing and turning back with one wind, and today by steam.

*Min faḍlihi* (of His bounty): that is, of God's bounty, through trade.

*An tamīda bikum* (lest it sway with you): that is, lest it tilt and move, so that what is upon it is destroyed and falls.

*Lā tuḥṣūhā* (you cannot count them): that is, you could not count them and keep track of them, let alone thank the Bestower, may He be exalted.

*Mā tusirrūna wa mā tu'linūn* (what you conceal and what you proclaim): this refers to the plotting against the Prophet (ﷺ) and the harming of him openly. This is in regard to the people of Makkah, since the address first concerns them, but the wording is general, so God knows every secret and every open matter concerning anyone.

**The meaning of the verses:**

The noble context continues to mention the signs of God's power, knowledge, wisdom and mercy, signs that call for His Oneness, worship, thanks and remembrance. God, may He be exalted, says: ﴿And it is He who subjected the sea﴾, and the sea is every large body of water, whether sweet or salt. Its subjection means making diving in it easy and making ships sail upon it. His words ﴿that you may eat from it fresh flesh and extract from it ornaments that you wear﴾ explain the reason for subjecting the sea: that people may hunt fish from it to eat, and extract pearls and coral as adornment for their women. His words ﴿and you see the ships ploughing through it﴾ mean: you, O observer of the sea, see the ships cutting through the water, going and coming. His words ﴿and that you may seek [His bounty]﴾ mean: He subjected the sea and the ship so that you might seek provision through trade, by transporting goods and merchandise from region to region, and all of that is from God's bounty and favour. ﴿And that perhaps you may be grateful﴾ means: so that you may thank God. That is, He subjected these things for you so that you might obtain provision from God's bounty, and then eat and thank God for it. Thanks is given by praising God and acknowledging His blessing, and by spending His blessings in what pleases Him.

His words ﴿And He cast into the earth firm mountains﴾ mean: He placed in the earth mountains that are fixed, ﴿lest it sway with you﴾, meaning so that it does not sway with you. Its swaying is its tilting and movement, for if it moved, life could not be settled upon it or lived within it. His words ﴿and rivers﴾ mean: He made rivers flow for you in the earth, such as the Nile, the Euphrates and others. ﴿And roads﴾ means: He cut paths for you. ﴿That perhaps you may be guided﴾ means: to your dwellings in your lands. His words ﴿and landmarks﴾ mean: He made for you landmarks for the roads and signs, such as hills, valleys, trees, and everything by which one can find the way and the direction. His words ﴿and by the star﴾ mean: and by the stars ﴿they are guided﴾. Sea travellers cannot know the direction of their course at night except by the stars, and so too travellers in the deserts and valleys cannot know the direction of their journey except by the stars. That was before the existence of the marine compass, which came into being only by the light and guidance of the star.

His words in verse [17]: ﴿Is He who creates like one who does not create? Will you not then remember?﴾ are a great rebuke to those who insist on worshipping idols and argue in their defence and fight for them. Is the worship of Him who creates, provides and directs human life, namely God, Lord of the worlds, the same as the worship of one who creates nothing, provides nothing and directs nothing? His words ﴿and landmarks﴾ mean: He made for you landmarks for the roads and signs, such as hills, valleys, trees, and everything by which one can find the way and the direction. His words ﴿and by the star﴾ mean: and by the stars ﴿they are guided﴾. Sea travellers cannot know the direction of their course at night except by the stars, and so too travellers in the deserts and valleys cannot know the direction of their journey except by the stars. That was before the existence of the marine compass, which came into being only by the light and guidance of the star.

His words in verse [17]: ﴿Is He who creates like one who does not create? Will you not then remember?﴾ are a great rebuke to those who insist on worshipping idols and argue in their defence and fight for them. Is the worship of Him who creates, provides and directs human life, namely God, Lord of the worlds, the same as the worship of one who creates nothing, provides nothing and directs nothing? Who among the sensible would equate the Living, the Giver of life, the Doer of whatever He wills, the Bestower of all life, with stones and idols? Therefore He rebuked them by saying ﴿Will you not then remember?﴾, so that you may remember and know that the worship of idols is false and the worship of God is true, and so that you may repent to your Lord and submit to Him before the punishment comes upon you.

His words, may He be exalted: ﴿And if you were to count the favour of God, you could not enumerate it﴾. After enumerating in these verses the many blessings, He informs that if people wished to count God's blessings, they could not count them, let alone thank Him for them. For this reason He said ﴿Indeed, God is Forgiving and Merciful﴾. Were it not so, He would hold them to account for their shortcoming in thanking Him for His blessings upon them, and would strip those blessings from them when they disbelieve and fail to acknowledge the Bestower, may He be exalted. His words, may He be exalted: ﴿And God knows what you conceal and what you proclaim﴾. This is the last of the manifestations of power, knowledge, wisdom and blessing in this noble context. God alone knows the secrets and the open affairs of people, so He knows their needs and what their lives require. If they take Him as an enemy and disbelieve in Him, how can they feel safe about their lives? Since the address in this context is a call to the idolaters of Makkah to faith and Oneness, the verse is a warning to them that God knows their plotting against His Messenger, their scheming of evil against him, and their harming of him by day. It therefore carries a threat and a warning to the disbelievers of Makkah.

**Guidance from the verses:**

1. Explanation of the reason for provision: it is gratitude. God, glorified and exalted, provides so that He may be thanked.
2. Permissibility of eating fish and all creatures of the sea.
3. There is no *zakāh* (obligatory almsgiving) on pearls and coral, because they are women's adornment.
4. Comparison between the Living, the Creator, the All-Knowing, and the dead, created idols, to establish the falsehood of worshipping other than God, the Exalted, because one who creates is not like one who is created.
5. Man's inability to thank God for His blessings requires that he thank for what he is able to. The phrase "Al-ḥamdu lillāh" (All praise is for God) is the head of thanks, and acknowledging one's inability to thank fully is itself a form of thanks. Gratitude means spending blessings on that for which God bestowed them.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 16, verses 20–25:

Explanation of the words:

*Wa-hum yukhlaquna* (وهم يخلقون): i.e., they are carved from stone and other materials.

*Wa-ma yash'urna ayyana yub'athun* (وما يشعرون إيان يبعثون): i.e., the idols do not perceive nor know the time at which they will be raised, which is the Day of Resurrection. Nor will their worshippers be raised at that time apart from Allah.

*Qulubuhum munkiratun* (قلوبهم منكرة): i.e., their hearts deny the Oneness (of Allah), prophethood, resurrection and recompense.

*Wa-hum mustakbirun* (وهم مستكبرون): due to the darkness of their hearts through disbelief, they are arrogant.

*La jaram* (لا جرم): i.e., truly.

*Asatir al-awwalin* (أساطير الأولين): i.e., the lies of the ancients.

*Liyahmilu awzarahum* (ليحملوا أوزارهم): i.e., their sins on the Day of Resurrection.

*Ala sa'a ma yazirun* (ألا ساء ما يزرون): i.e., evil is what they bear of burdens.

Meaning of the verses:

In this context there is a clear confrontation with the polytheists after the evidences of their associating partners with Allah and their misguidance have already been presented. His saying, exalted is He, ﴿And those whom you invoke besides Allah﴾, i.e., those you worship, O polytheists, ﴿are dead, not alive﴾, i.e., they are dead, for they have no life. The proof of that is that they neither hear, nor see, nor speak. His saying, ﴿And they do not perceive when they will be resurrected﴾, i.e., they do not know when they will be raised, just as you, O worshippers of them, do not perceive when you will be raised. So how can their worship be valid, when they are dead and do not know when they will be raised for questioning, interrogation, and recompense for what was earned in this life? His saying, ﴿Your God is one God﴾, is the rational conclusion which sensible people do not deny: that the one worshipped is One with no partner, and He is Allah, majestic is His majesty, for He is the Creator, the Provider, the Manager, the Giver of life and the Causer of death, possessor of the sublime attributes and the most beautiful names. Whatever else there is does not create, does not provide, does not manage, does not give life, and does not cause death, so deifying it is folly and misguidance. After establishing the divinity of Allah, exalted is He, and affirming it by sound logic, He, exalted is He, said: ﴿As for those who do not believe in the Hereafter, their hearts are denying, and they are arrogant﴾. This mentions the cause of disbelief among the disbelievers and of corruption among the corrupters, which is their denial of the final resurrection, for a servant cannot remain upright upon the path of truth and goodness if he does not believe in the Last Day, the Day of recompense for deeds done in the worldly life. He, exalted is He, informs that those who do not believe in the Hereafter have hearts that deny everything of the truth they hear, which the Messenger of Allah ﷺ calls to and which the verses of the Noble Qur'an make clear. Together with the denial of their hearts to what they hear of the truth, they are arrogant against accepting the truth and submitting to it. His saying, exalted is He, ﴿Undoubtedly, Allah knows what they conceal and what they reveal. Indeed, He does not love the arrogant﴾, i.e., truly, Allah knows what those who deny the Hereafter conceal and what they disclose, and He will count it against them and recompense them for it without doubt, on a Day in which they used to deny. ... Alas for regret, and alas for remorse!! This recompense is the punishment of the Fire, caused by Allah's hatred of the arrogant and His not loving them. His saying, exalted is He, ﴿And when it is said to them, "What has your Lord sent down?" they say, "The tales of the ancients"﴾: He, exalted is He, informs about those whose hearts deny the divine revelation and what the Messenger of Allah brought. These arrogant people, when asked about the Qur'an by someone who wishes to know, from those who heard of the Muhammadan call and came from distant lands to learn about it, would say, "Tales of the ancients", i.e., false reports about the ancients, written down among people, which he relates and holds to be true. By this they turn people away from Islam and bar them from the way of Allah. He, exalted is He, said: ﴿So that they may bear their burdens﴾, i.e., the full consequence of their sins and the consequence of the sins of those they barred from the way of Allah, complete and unreduced, on the Day of Resurrection. They do not know this, but the reality is: whoever calls to misguidance bears its burden, and the burden of those who act upon it is not reduced in any way; likewise, whoever calls to guidance has the reward of those who act upon it, and their reward is not reduced in any way. His saying, exalted is He, ﴿Unquestionably, evil is what they bear﴾, i.e., how wretched is the burden they carry, for it leads them to the Fire and destroys them in the fire of Hell.

Guidance of the verses:

From the guidance of these verses:

1- The nullity of polytheism and the affirmation of monotheism.

2- Denial of the Last Day, resurrection and recompense is the cause of every evil and corruption a servant commits.

3- Condemnation of the crime of arrogance against the truth and submission to it.

4- Clarification of the sin and consequence of one who bars people from the way of Allah by turning them away from Islam.

5- Clarification of the consequence of one who calls to misguidance: he bears the burden of everyone who acts upon it.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 16, verses 26–34:

Explanation of the words:

"من قبلهم" (min qablihim): i.e., before the disbelievers of Quraysh in Makkah, such as Nimrod and others.

"فأتى الله بنيانهم" (fa-atā Allāhu bunyānahum): i.e., He targeted it to destroy it, so He sent upon it wind and earthquake, and it collapsed from its foundations.

"وخر عليهم السقف" (wa-kharra ʿalayhimu al-saqf): i.e., it fell because the foundations gave way and collapsed.

"كنتم تشاقون فيهم" (kuntum tushāqqūna fīhim): i.e., you opposed the believers regarding them by your worship of them and your disputing on their behalf, and you opposed Allah by abandoning His worship and worshipping them.

"وقال الذين أوتوا العلم" (wa-qāla alladhīna ūtu al-ʿilm): i.e., the prophets and the believers.

"ظالمي أنفسهم" (ẓālimī anfusihim): by shirk and sins.

"فألقوا السلم" (fa-alqaw al-salam): i.e., they submitted and surrendered.

"فلبئس مثوى المتكبرين" (fa-la-bi'sa mathwā al-mutakabbirīn): i.e., how evil is the abode of the arrogant in Hell, for example.

"وقيل للذين اتقوا" (wa-qīla lilladhīna ittaqaw): i.e., who guarded against shirk and sins.

"للذين أحسنوا" (lilladhīna aḥsanū): i.e., their deeds, words and intentions, which they performed in accordance with the will of Allah the Exalted.

"حسنة" (ḥasanah): i.e., the good life, a life of honor and dignity.

"ولنعم دار المتقين" (wa-la-niʿma dāru al-muttaqīn): i.e., Paradise, the abode of peace.

"طيبين" (ṭayyibīn): i.e., the souls, through what they purified them with of faith and righteous deeds, and through what they kept them far from of shirk and sins.

"يقولون سلام عليكم" (yaqūlūna salāmun ʿalaykum): i.e., the Angel of Death, ʿAzrāʾīl, and his helpers say to them.

"هل ينظرون إلا أن تأتيهم الملائكة" (hal yanẓurūna illā an ta'tiyahumu al-malā'ikah): i.e., to seize their souls, and at that point they will believe.

"أو يأتي أمر ربك" (aw yaʾtiya amru rabbika): i.e., with the punishment, or with the establishment of the Hour and their gathering before Allah, Mighty and Majestic.

"وحاق بهم ما كانوا به يستهزئون" (wa-ḥāqa bihim mā kānū bihi yastahzi'ūn): i.e., the punishment descended upon them and encompassed them, while they had been mocking it.

Meaning of the verses:

The noble context continues with the disbelievers of Quraysh, admonishing and enlightening them about the ignorance and misguidance they are in. He, the Exalted, says: ﴿Those before them had already plotted⦆, i.e., before the plotting of the disbelievers of Quraysh, such as Nimrod, Pharaoh and other tyrants who exalted themselves against Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, and plotted against their messengers. Nimrod cast Abraham into the fire, and Pharaoh said, "Leave me to kill Moses, and let him call upon his Lord." And His saying: ﴿So Allah came at their structure from its foundations⦆, i.e., the command of Allah came to demolish it and bring it down upon the oppressive tyrants. ﴿So the roof fell upon them from above them, and the punishment came to them from where they did not perceive⦆. Their falsehood departed and their plotting ceased. Has not this admonished the disbelievers of Quraysh, who plot against their prophet and devise evil against him by killing, exile or imprisonment? And His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿Then on the Day of Resurrection He will disgrace them⦆, i.e., He will humiliate, abase and rebuke them, saying: ﴿"Where are My partners about whom you used to dispute?"⦆, i.e., your idols and images about whom you opposed Me by worshipping them instead of Me, just as you opposed My righteous believers, i.e., you opposed them in that and fought against them concerning it. Here the witnesses and those given knowledge, from among the prophets and the scholars devoted to the Lord, will say: ﴿Indeed, disgrace today and misfortune are upon the disbelievers⦆, i.e., indeed, humiliation, degradation and lowliness are upon the disbelievers. And His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿Those whom the angels take in death while they are wronging themselves⦆ by shirk and sins. Among the sins is abandoning emigration and remaining among disbelievers and corrupt criminals, where the believer cannot worship Allah, the Exalted, by abandoning sins and performing acts of worship. And His saying ﴿So they will offer submission⦆, i.e., upon witnessing the Angel of Death and his helpers, they submitted and surrendered, and tried to excuse themselves with lies, saying ﴿"We did not do any evil"⦆. The angels will respond to them, saying: ﴿"Yes, indeed; Allah is Knowing of what you used to do"⦆, i.e., you used to do evil. It will also be said to them: ﴿"Enter the gates of Hell, to abide therein. And wretched is the residence of the arrogant"⦆, i.e., the abode and dwelling of those arrogant toward the worship of Allah alone.

And His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿It will be said to those who feared Allah⦆, i.e., their Lord, so they did not associate anything with Him, did not disobey Him in His command or prohibition, and obeyed His Messenger likewise: ﴿"What has your Lord sent down?"⦆, i.e., when someone who came to Makkah to learn about the message of Islam asked them, they would say to him: ﴿"Good."⦆, i.e., He has sent down good, because the Qur'an is good and was sent down with good, unlike the students of the polytheists who say "legends of the ancients," as has preceded in this context.

Having mentioned the recompense of the disbelievers and the punishment they will meet in the Fire of Hell, those who wronged themselves in this worldly life by their shirk with Allah, their scheming and their wrongdoing against the believers, He mentioned the recompense of the good-doers. He said: ﴿For those who did good⦆, i.e., they believed and did righteous deeds following the law of Allah in that, so they sincerely devoted their worship to Allah the Exalted, called people to worship Allah, and urged them to it, thereby being good to themselves and to others. For those who did good in this world there is ﴿a good⦆, which is the good life, the life of purity, honor and dignity. And the dwelling of the Hereafter is better for them than the dwelling of this world, along with what good there is in it. And His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿And how excellent is the home of the righteous⦆ is praise and commendation of that Hereafter abode, because of the lasting bliss in it. Its attribution to the righteous is in view of their being its rightful inhabitants, since it is specific to them, which they inherited through their faith and righteous deeds, by abandoning shirk and sins.

And His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿Gardens of perpetual residence which they will enter, beneath which rivers flow; for them therein is whatever they wish⦆ is a description and clarification of the abode of the righteous. He informs that they are gardens, plural of garden (jannah), which is an orchard containing trees, rivers, palaces, and whatever is delicious and pleasing of foods, drinks, clothing, spouses and mounts. And His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿For them therein is whatever they wish⦆ is the utmost in honor and bounty, for the servant finding everything he desires and seeks is a bliss to which nothing can be added. And His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿Thus does Allah reward the righteous⦆, i.e., like this good, magnificent recompense, Allah rewards the righteous in this world and the Hereafter. And His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿Those whom the angels take in death while they are good⦆, i.e., pure of soul; their souls have a good fragrance, the fruit of their faith and righteous deeds, and the result of their keeping far from what defiles them of the filth of shirk and the rot of sins. And His saying: ﴿They will say⦆, i.e., the angels, who are the Angel of Death and his helpers, will say to them: ﴿"Peace be upon you"⦆, greeting them, and in that is good news for them of their Lord's pleasure and His noble neighborhood. ﴿"Enter Paradise"⦆ with your souls today, and with your bodies tomorrow on the Day of Resurrection. And His saying: ﴿for what you used to do⦆, i.e., because of what you used to do of acts of obedience and racing in good deeds, after your hearts had acted by faith, certainty, love for Allah, hatred for what opposes Him, desire for Him and reliance upon Him, the Mighty and Majestic. This is what the verses [31, 32] contained. As for the verses after that, Allah, rebuking the slowness of Quraysh's faith and repentance after those proofs, evidences, indications and clear signs upon the truthfulness of the prophethood of Muhammad ﷺ, and upon the obligation of monotheism and the invalidity of shirk, and upon belief in the Last Day, says:

﴿Do they await except that the angels come to them⦆, i.e., they await nothing after this except that the angels come to seize their souls, ﴿or that the command of your Lord comes⦆ with their destruction and eradication, since there remains nothing for them to await except one of these two matters, and both are bitter and evil for them.

And His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿Thus did those before them⦆ of the disbelieving nations before them, so the vengeance of Allah befell them, His punishment descended upon them, and He destroyed them. ﴿And Allah did not wrong them⦆, Exalted is He, in that at all, ﴿but they were wronging themselves⦆ by their persistence in shirk, obstinacy, denial and arrogant rejection. ﴿So the evil consequences of what they did struck them⦆, i.e., the recompense of the evil deeds of disbelief and wrongdoing they had done. ﴿And there encompassed them⦆, i.e., descended upon them and surrounded them, ﴿what they used to mock⦆, since when their messengers warned them of the punishment of Allah, they scoffed at them, mocked the punishment and made light of it, until it descended upon them, and we seek refuge in Allah, the Exalted.

From the guidance of the verses:

1- The evil outcome of plotting, and that it inevitably falls upon its people; the intended meaning is evil plotting.

2- Explanation of Allah's disgrace on the Day of Resurrection for the people of shirk with Him and of disobedience to Him and to His Messenger.

3- The virtue of the people of knowledge, as they are taken as witnesses on the Day of Resurrection, and they will mock the people of the Fire.

4- Explanation of the submission of wrongdoers at death, their defeat and their lies.

5- Affirmation of the belief in resurrection and the Hereafter in the most eloquent, wise and firm manner.

6- Applying the word "good" to the Qur'an, which is truly good; whoever is given the Qur'an has been given all good, so one should not regard anyone of worldly people as better than him, lest he resent Allah's blessing upon him.

7- The felicity of both abodes for the people of ihsan, who are the people of faith and Islam; their ihsan in faith is through sincerity, and in Islam through conformity to the Sharia and vigilance of Allah in that.

8- Glad tidings for the people of faith and piety at death, and upon rising from the graves, with lasting bliss in the presence of the Lord of the worlds.

9- The deeds of the hearts and limbs are a cause of entering Paradise, not a price for it, for it is too precious; rather, deeds purify the self and cleanse the soul, and thereby the servant becomes fit to enter Paradise.

10- What the criminals await through their persistence in injustice, evil and corruption is nothing but punishment, sooner or later; it will surely befall them as a decreed matter, unless they hasten to sincere repentance.

Meaning of the verses:

The noble context continues with the disbelievers of Quraysh, admonishing and enlightening them about the ignorance and misguidance they are in. Among the sins is abandoning emigration and remaining among disbelievers and corrupt criminals, where the believer cannot worship Allah, the Exalted, by abandoning sins and performing acts of worship. And His saying ﴿So they will offer submission⦆, i.e., upon witnessing the Angel of Death and his helpers, they submitted and surrendered, and tried to excuse themselves with lies, saying ﴿"We did not do any evil"⦆. 3- The virtue of the people of knowledge, as they are taken as witnesses on the Day of Resurrection, and they will mock the people of the Fire.

4- Explanation of the submission of wrongdoers at death, their defeat and their lies.

5- Affirmation of the belief in resurrection and the Hereafter in the most eloquent, wise and firm manner.

6- Applying the word "good" to the Qur'an, which is truly good; whoever is given the Qur'an has been given all good, so one should not regard anyone of worldly people as better than him, lest he resent Allah's blessing upon him.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 16, verses 35–40:

Explanation of the words:

"And those who associated [others with Allah] said" — they are the disbelievers of Quraysh and their polytheists.

"Nor would we have prohibited anything without Him" — such as the sawa'ib (free-roaming animals), the bahira (slit-eared she-camel), the wasila (ewe that bears twins in succession) and the ham (stallion camel freed after a set number of services).

"Is there upon the messengers except the clear notification?" — meaning: there is upon the messengers only the clear notification; the interrogative here is for negation.

"And avoid the taghut" — meaning: the worship of idols and images.

"Upon him the misguidance was justly due" — meaning: it was decreed in Allah's eternal knowledge from before time.

"Their most emphatic oaths" — meaning: the utmost of their oaths, where they exerted their effort in swearing, exaggerating.

"[It is] a promise binding upon Him in truth" — meaning: yes, He will resurrect whoever has died; He has promised it as a promise and made it a binding truth, so it will certainly occur without doubt.

"About which they differ" — meaning: among the believers, concerning monotheism and polytheism.

"That they had been liars" — meaning: in their saying, "We will not be resurrected after death."

Meaning of the verses:

The discourse continues in argument with the polytheists of Quraysh. Did they say this out of faith in the will of Allah, or did they say it mockingly and derisively, defending their polytheism and their false legislation in prohibition and permission according to their whims? Both possibilities are open. The response to them comes in two parts. The first: since Allah has forbidden them from polytheism and legislating, this is the greatest proof of His prohibition of their polytheism and their prohibited things such as the sawa'ib, the bahira and others. The second: that He has not punished them for these things yet does not prove His approval of them, as evidenced by the fact that the disbelieving nations before them said the same statement, citing it in support of their falsehood, and yet they were not long before Allah seized them. This definitively shows His disapproval of their polytheism and their legislation, as He said in Surah al-An'am in refutation of this doubt: ﴿Thus did those before them,﴾ until they tasted Our might — that is, the punishment of Our vengeance upon them, because they denied Our messengers and fabricated against Us. His saying ﴿Thus did those who were before them﴾ — from the earlier nations — said the same to their messengers and did the same deeds, until Allah seized them with punishment. His saying ﴿Then upon the messengers is nothing but the clear notification﴾ means: it is not upon the Messenger to compel the polytheists to abandon polytheism nor to oblige them to the law; rather, he is only to convey to them the command and prohibition of Allah, nothing more. Therefore, in general, this is a consolation to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and a means of encouraging him to be patient until he conveys the call of his Lord and is given victory over his enemies. This is what the first verse of this context indicates [35]. As for His saying in the second verse [36]: ﴿And We did certainly send into every nation a messenger, [saying], "Worship Allah and avoid taghut"﴾ — He informs that He has not left any nation without sending a messenger to it to guide it, to clarify the path to its salvation, and to warn it against the ways of its misguidance and destruction. He also informs of the unity of the call among the messengers, which is "There is no deity except Allah," explained as worshipping Allah alone and avoiding the taghut, which is everything worshipped besides Allah, to which Satan has called by beautifying and adorning worship through whispering on one hand, and through his allies among humankind on the other.

As for His saying ﴿So among them is one whom Allah guided﴾ — meaning, from among the nations to which they were sent — ﴿and among them is one upon whom misguidance was justly due﴾ — He knew from eternity in the Book of Decrees, because he persisted in misguidance, argued for it and fought on its behalf by his own choice and free will, so Allah deprived him of that success and he went astray into a misguidance for which there is no hope of guidance. His saying: ﴿So travel through the earth and observe how was the end of the deniers﴾ is a command to the disbelieving Quraysh who argued in falsehood and defended their polytheism and their false legislation: that they should travel through the earth, southward or northward, and observe how was the end of those who denied, like them — from the people of 'Ad in the south, Thamud in the north, and Midian, Lut and Pharaoh in the west. His saying ﴿Indeed, Allah does not guide those who are misguided﴾ means no one can guide whom Allah has led astray, because Allah's leading astray occurs according to specific laws that do not accept substitution or alteration, owing to the strength of His authority and the vastness of His wisdom. His saying ﴿And they will have no helpers﴾ means: those misguided ones whom Allah has led astray, according to His sunnah, will have no helpers to support them against the punishment that will befall them and the loss and deprivation that will come upon them. This is what His saying in verse [40] indicates: ﴿Indeed, Our word to a thing when We intend it is only that We say to it, "Be," and it is.﴾ Let no speaker say: how is one addressing what does not exist, commanding it to come into being? Indeed, when Allah wills a thing, He first knows it, then says to it "Be," and it is.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 16, verses 41–44:

Explanation of the words:

﴿Those who emigrated for the sake of Allah﴾: that is, they left Makkah in the way of Allah, to support His religion and establish it among people.

﴿We will surely settle them in this world in a good place﴾: that is, We will surely settle them in a good abode, which is the Prophet's city (Madinah). This is with regard to those about whom the verse was revealed.

﴿Those who were patient and upon their Lord they rely﴾: that is, they endured the harm of the polytheists, and they emigrated relying upon their Lord in their land of emigration.

﴿So ask the people of the Reminder﴾: that is, O you who doubt what Muhammad ﷺ brought, ask the people of the Torah and the Gospel to remove your doubt and to bring you to the truth, and that what Muhammad brought is true, and that all the messengers before him were human beings like him.

﴿With clear proofs and scriptures﴾: that is, We sent them as human beings with clear proofs and scriptures to guide people.

﴿And We have sent down to you the Reminder﴾: that is, the Qur'an.

﴿So that you may make clear to people what has been sent down to them﴾: a reason for sending down the Reminder, since explaining (al-bayan) is the function of the messengers.

Meaning of the verses:

After the harm against the believers intensified because of the obstinacy and tyranny of the polytheists, Allah the Exalted, through His Messenger, permitted the believers to emigrate from Makkah to Abyssinia, and then to Madinah. Men and women emigrated. Thus Allah the Exalted praised them and encouraged emigration from the house of disbelief, saying, the Mighty and Majestic: ﴿And those who emigrated for the sake of Allah﴾, that is, for the sake of Allah's essence, and for the sake of worshipping Allah and supporting His religion, ﴿after they had been wronged﴾, that is, by the polytheists, ﴿We will surely settle them﴾, that is, We will surely house them and lodge them, ﴿in this world a good abode﴾, which is the Prophet's city, and We will provide them therein with good provision. This is with regard to those about whom the verse was revealed; otherwise, every person who emigrates for the sake of Allah, the Lord fulfils this promise for him, as He said: ﴿And whoever emigrates in the way of Allah will find on earth many a refuge and abundance﴾ [An-Nisa: 100], that is, in livelihood and provision. ﴿And the reward of the Hereafter is greater, if they only knew﴾, prepared for those who emigrate in the way of Allah. This is an encouragement to emigration and an exhortation to those who are slow to emigrate. His saying: ﴿Those who were patient and upon their Lord they rely﴾ is a description of their condition and praise of them with goodness, because they were patient first over the harm in Makkah; when they were permitted to emigrate, they emigrated relying upon Allah the Exalted, entrusting their affairs to Him and trusting in His promise. This is what the two verses [41] and [42] indicate. As for the third verse [43] and the fourth of this context, they establish a factual truth after refuting the doubt of the polytheists who said, "How could Allah send Muhammad as a messenger when he is a human being like us? He did not send an angel..." This is what Allah the Exalted informed of in His saying: ﴿And We did not send before you except men﴾, that is, of the messengers, ﴿not angels﴾, ﴿to whom We revealed﴾ by Our command. And His saying: ﴿So ask the people of the Reminder﴾, O polytheists who deny that the Messenger may be a human being, ask the people of the Reminder, which is the former Book, that is, ask the scholars of the People of the Book, the Jews and the Christians, whether Allah the Exalted ever sent messengers other than human beings, ﴿if you do not know﴾, for they will inform you. Moses and Jesus were none but human beings. His saying: ﴿with clear proofs and scriptures﴾, that is, We sent those messengers, being human, with clear proofs, meaning the evidences and indications showing the obligation to worship Us and to abandon the worship of others besides Us, and scriptures, meaning books. Then Allah the Exalted says to His Messenger: ﴿And We have sent down to you the Reminder so that you may make clear to people what has been sent down to them﴾, and in this is an affirmation of his prophethood. His saying: ﴿so that they may reflect﴾ means they would recognise the truth of what you brought them and believe, and turn in repentance to their Lord, and thus be saved and attain happiness.

Guidance from the verses:

From the guidance of the verses:

1- The virtue of emigration and its obligation when a believer is persecuted and unable to worship Allah the Exalted.

2- The obligation to ask people of knowledge for everyone who does not know the matters of his religion, whether belief, worship or rulings.

3- The Sunnah is indispensable, for it is what explains the general (mujmal) statements of the Qur'an and clarifies its meanings.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 16, verses 45–50:

Explanation of the Words:

*Makaru as-sayyi'at* (they plotted the evil schemes): meaning, they devised evil plots, so "evil" (sayyi'at) is a description of the schemes they plotted.

*Fi taqallubihim* (in their going back and forth): meaning, in the lands, traveling for trade and other purposes.

*Ala takhawwuf* (by gradual reduction): meaning, by diminishing.

*Yatafayya'u zilaluhu* (their shadows incline): meaning, they turn from one side to another.

*Sujjadan lillah* (prostrating to Allah): meaning, submissive to Allah as He wills of them.

*Dakhirun* (humbled): meaning, abject and degraded.

*Min fawqihim* (above them): meaning, above them, for He, exalted is He, is above everything in His essence, authority and dominion.

*Ma yu'marun* (what they are commanded): meaning, what their Lord, exalted is He, commands them.

Meaning of the Verses:

The context continues to warn the polytheists and remind them, so that perhaps they will return by repentance from polytheism and from denying the Prophethood, the Resurrection and the Recompense. Allah, exalted is He, says: ﴿Do then those who plot evil deeds feel secure﴾ — the plots: including the attempt to kill the Prophet (ﷺ), polytheism, denial of Prophethood and the Resurrection, wronging the believers and torturing some of them — have they felt secure ﴿that Allah will cause the earth to swallow them﴾ from beneath them so that they sink into its depths, ﴿or that the punishment will come upon them from where they do not perceive﴾ and do not expect, such as a violent wind that sweeps them away, or a plague that encompasses them, or a drought that takes away their wealth. And His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Or He seizes them in their going back and forth﴾ means in their trade and journeys, going and returning from one land to another. ﴿Then they cannot escape﴾ from Him, exalted is He, if He wills to seize and destroy them. And His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Or He seizes them by gradual reduction﴾ means diminishing, by destroying them one by one or group after group until none of them remains; He has already seized some of them at Badr and at Uhud. And His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Indeed, your Lord is Kind and Merciful﴾ is a reminder to them of His kindness and mercy, for had it not been for these two, He would have sent down His vengeance upon them and made them taste His punishment without respite for repentance or delay for returning to the truth. And His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Have they not considered what things Allah has created﴾ of trees, mountains, humans and animals, ﴿whose shadows incline﴾ in the morning and evening ﴿from the right and the left﴾ — "plural of shimal" — ﴿prostrating to Allah﴾ submissively with their shadows ﴿while they are humbled﴾, meaning abject and degraded. Is this not sufficient for them as evidence of their submission to Allah and their humility before Him, so that they would believe in Him, worship Him and affirm His oneness, thereby being saved from His punishment and attaining His mercy? And His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And to Allah prostrates whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth of creatures﴾ — meaning, to Allah alone, not to other than Him, prostrates (in the sense of submitting and yielding to what Allah wills of life or death, health or sickness, good or otherwise) every creature that crawls upon this earth; ﴿and the angels﴾, despite their nobility, prostrate, ﴿and they are not arrogant﴾ in worshiping their Lord, ﴿they fear their Lord above them﴾ for He is the Most High, the Supreme, and all creation is beneath Him, ﴿and they do what they are commanded﴾, so they do not disobey their Lord in what He commands them. If this is the state of the angels, then what is the matter with these polytheists that they persist in corruption, arrogance, denial and obstinacy, when they are the most contemptible of all creatures and the worst of created beings, if they remain upon their disbelief and polytheism?

Guidance from the Verses:

From the guidance of these verses:

1- The prohibition of feeling secure from the plot of Allah.

2- Everything prostrates to Allah, meaning it submits to what He wills of them; however, voluntary and deliberate prostration is what the servant is rewarded for, whereas involuntary obedience carries neither reward nor punishment.

3- The virtue of voluntary and deliberate prostration.

4- The legitimacy of prostration at this verse: when the reciter or listener recites or hears: ﴿they fear their Lord above them and do what they are commanded﴾, he should prostrate if he is in a state of purity, facing the qibla if possible, and he says tasbih in the prostration and takbir when lowering and raising, and he does not say the salam; and he does not prostrate at sunrise or at sunset.

Explanation of the words:

﴿Do not take two gods﴾: i.e., do not worship them, since you have only one God.

﴿And to Him belongs whatever is in the heavens and the earth﴾: i.e., by creation and dominion. Therefore, what you worship besides God belongs to God, and He has not permitted its worship.

﴿And to Him is religion, due and enduring﴾: i.e., sincere, perpetual, and obligatory.

﴿Then to Him you cry out for help﴾: i.e., you raise your voices in supplication to Him, seeking relief from Him.

﴿Enjoy yourselves; you will soon know﴾: a warning for their disbelief, their association of partners, and their forgetting the supplication of God, the Exalted.

﴿And they assign to what they do not know a share﴾: i.e., they assign to their gods a share of the crops and livestock.

﴿Of what you used to invent﴾: i.e., what you fabricate with lies and invent against God, the Mighty and Majestic.

Meaning of the verses:

After establishing the proofs of monotheism and the falsehood of association, He informed them that God is their Lord, the Lord of everything, and said to them: O people, ﴿And God said: Do not take two gods; He is but one God﴾. The word "two" emphasises the word "gods": that is, do not worship two gods, but worship one God, who is God, for there is no god but Him. So how can you take two gods when He is ﴿one God﴾ and no other, the Creator, the Provider, the Owner? And how can what is among His creatures be equated with Him and worshipped alongside Him? His saying, the Exalted, ﴿So fear Me alone﴾: i.e., fear Me alone and do not fear other than Me, for in My hand is everything, and no one else has anything. I am the one who gives life and causes death, who harms and benefits. He rebukes them for fearing other than Him, the Glorified and Exalted, one who does not deserve to be feared, because of his inability and lack of power to benefit or harm. His saying, the Exalted, ﴿And to Him belongs whatever is in the heavens and the earth﴾ is a proof of the falsehood of fearing or desiring anything other than Him, since to Him belongs whatever is in the heavens and the earth by creation and dominion. His saying ﴿And to Him is religion, enduring﴾: i.e., worship and obedience are perpetual, constant, and obligatory. Surely, to God belongs pure religion. His saying, the Exalted: ﴿Is it other than God you fear?﴾ rebukes them for fearing other than Him, when He is the One who must be feared and dreaded, for He is the true King, able to bestow blessings and their means. How can one fear him who possesses no harm or benefit, and disobey Him in whose hand is everything, and to whom all things return? What He wills comes to be, and what He does not will does not come to be. His saying ﴿And whatever blessing you have is from God﴾: the Exalted informs them of the reality they deny. He tells them that whatever blessing they have, great or small, of health, wealth, or children, is from God, their Creator and the Giver of their lives, and not from anyone other than Him. He supports this with their innate awareness: when harm touches them, such as poverty, sickness, or a change of circumstance like the fear of drowning at sea, they raise their voices to the utmost, calling upon God and asking Him to remove their harm or deliver them from the destruction they expect. So the Mighty and Majestic says: ﴿Then when harm touches you, to Him﴾ alone, ﴿you cry out﴾ by raising your voices in supplication and appeal to Him, the Glorified and Exalted. And His saying: ﴿Then when He removes the harm from you, behold, a group﴾ large ﴿of you associate others with their Lord﴾, worshipping other than Him in various kinds of worship, forgetting God who removed their harm and delivered them from their destruction.

His saying: ﴿So that they may deny what We have given them﴾: i.e., so that their affair results in ingratitude and forgetfulness of what God gave them of blessings and what He delivered them from in trials. Is this how recompense should be? He bestows every kind of blessing and delivers from every distress, and then they forget all of that for Him and worship other than Him? Rather, they even wage war against His religion and His Messenger? Thus, ﴿Enjoy yourselves﴾, O disbelievers, ﴿for you will soon know﴾ the outcome of your disbelief and your turning away from obeying God, remembering Him, and thanking Him. His saying, the Exalted: ﴿And they assign to what they do not know a share of what We have provided them﴾: this mentions another of their defects and another of their falsehoods, that they assign to their idols, about which they know nothing of benefit or harm, giving or withholding, causing death or life, a share and portion of their wealth by which they seek nearness to them, as obedience to Satan. They therefore set free the she-camels (sawa'ib) for them, and cut the ears of the livestock (baha'ir) for them, and likewise assigned to them a share of the tilth and the orchards, as is mentioned in Surat al-An'am and before it in al-Ma'idah. His saying, the Exalted: ﴿By God, you will certainly be questioned about what you used to invent﴾: the Almighty swore to them as a threat and a warning that they will be questioned on the Day of Resurrection about what they used to fabricate, that is, this false legislation, by which they prohibit and permit, and give their gods what they wish. He will rebuke them for it and recompense them with Hell, and wretched is the resting place.

2. The obligation to fear God alone and no other.
3. The obligation to make religion sincerely for God, since He is the true God and no other.
4. Every blessing, great or small, that a servant has is from God, the Glorified and Exalted.
5. A warning to the polytheists if they persist in their association and do not repent.
6. Condemnation of the polytheists and their false legislation of permitting, prohibiting, giving, and withholding.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 16, verses 57–62:

Explanation of the words:

*Wa yajʿaluna lillahi al-banat* (And they attribute daughters to Allah): that is, when they said the angels are the daughters of Allah.

*Wa lahum ma yashtahun* (And for themselves what they desire): that is, the males among the children.

*Zalla wajhuhu muswaddan* (His face remains darkened): that is, changed by blackness because of the distress upon him.

*Wa huwa kazim* (And he is suppressed with grief): that is, filled with sorrow.

*Am yadussuhu fi al-turab* (Or bury her in the dust): that is, bury that female infant alive, which is the wa'd (infanticide).

*Mathal al-su'* (The evil description): that is, the ugly attribute.

*Wa lillahi al-mathal al-a'la* (And to Allah belongs the highest description): that is, the supreme attribute, which is "There is no god but Allah."

*Anna lahumu al-husna* (That for them is the best reward): that is, Paradise, as one of them said: "And if I am returned to my Lord, surely I will have with Him the best (reward)."

*Wa annahum mufratun* (And that they will be sent forward): that is, brought forward to Hell and left there.

Explanation of the verses:

The context continues to clarify the errors of the polytheists in their beliefs and conduct. Allah the Exalted says: ﴿And they attribute to Allah daughters, glory be to Him, while for themselves is what they desire﴾. This is among the worst of their statements and the most corrupt of their beliefs, for they attribute daughters to Allah, saying the angels are the daughters of Allah, while at the same time they detest having daughters attributed to themselves. When one of them is given the news of a female child, that is, he is told that a daughter has been born to him, his day is spent in complete distress and sorrow, ﴿his face darkened, and he is suppressed with grief﴾, filled with sorrow and anxiety. ﴿He hides himself from the people﴾, that is, he conceals himself and disappears from the eyes of people out of fear of disgrace, ﴿because of the evil of that which he has been given news of﴾, which is the daughter. In this matter he stands between two choices regarding this newborn: either he keeps her, ﴿upon humiliation﴾, that is, in disgrace and degradation, keeping her in his house among his children, or he ﴿buries her in the dust﴾, that is, buries her alive, which is the well-known wa'd among them. Allah the Exalted denounces this crime: ﴿Unquestionably, evil is what they decide﴾. In their judgment in this matter, both in attributing daughters to Allah while disowning them for themselves, and in burying daughters or demeaning them, their jahili judgment is an evil judgment. This is what the first verse [57] indicates, which is His saying: ﴿And they attribute to Allah daughters﴾, where they said the angels are the daughters of Allah. ﴿Glory be to Him﴾, that is, the Exalted has declared Himself free from having a child or a consort; it is not fitting for Him to have a child, whether male or female, because He is the Lord and Owner of everything, so what need would He have of a child?

The second verse [58] is His saying: ﴿And when one of them is given news of a female, his face becomes darkened﴾, that is, he spends the whole day with a face darkened from grief, ﴿and he is suppressed with grief﴾, that is, filled with sorrow and anxiety. ﴿He hides himself from the people because of the evil of what he has been given news of﴾, that is, of the daughter. ﴿Shall he keep her in humiliation or bury her in the dust? Unquestionably, evil is what they decide.﴾

His saying: ﴿For those who do not believe in the Hereafter is the description of evil﴾ informs that those who do not believe in the Hereafter, that is, those who deny the final resurrection, have the evil description, that is, the evil attribute. This is because of their ignorance and the darkness of their souls, for they do no good and abstain from no evil, since they do not believe in reckoning and recompense. Those people have the worst attribute in everything. ﴿And to Allah belongs the highest description﴾, that is, the supreme attribute, which is that there is no god but Him, free from all deficiencies, Lord and Owner of everything, in whose hand is good, and He is over all things capable, having no partner, no equal, and no offspring. His saying: ﴿And He is the Exalted in Might, the Wise﴾ is praise of Himself with the greatest attributes: might, dominance, and supremacy over everything, and supreme wisdom in His management and direction of the affairs of His servants. His judgment and decree belong to Him; there is no god but Him and no lord besides Him.

His saying in verse [61]: ﴿And if Allah were to seize the people for their wrongdoing, He would not leave upon it [the earth] any creature﴾, that is, upon the earth, ﴿any moving creature﴾, that is, any living soul moving upon the earth, whether human or animal. This is the reason for not seizing those who do not believe in the Hereafter while they cause corruption and commit crimes. This delay follows from high wisdoms, which He indicated by His saying: ﴿But He delays them until a specified term﴾, that is, a fixed, determined time, which may be the end of each person's life, or may be the end of life as a whole. When that term comes, they cannot delay from it an hour, nor can they advance it an hour. Then He will recompense them for their evil deeds with their like, and your Lord is never unjust to the servants.

The last verse of this context [62] contains a denunciation of the evil state of those who do not believe in the Hereafter. Because of their ignorance of Allah and the ugliness of their conception of Him, and their wrongdoing to their own souls, they attribute to Allah what they themselves detest, namely daughters and partners, and they revile and disparage the Messenger. Yet despite this, they boastfully lie that they will have the best reward, that is, Paradise, on the Day of Resurrection. Allah the Exalted refutes this fabrication and this foolish nonsense by His saying: ﴿Without doubt, for them is the Fire﴾, instead of Paradise, ﴿and they will be sent forward﴾, that is, brought forward to it and left there forever. This is what the verse contains in His saying: ﴿And they attribute to Allah what they dislike, and their tongues describe the lie that for them is the best (reward). Without doubt, for them is the Fire, and they will be sent forward﴾. If *mufratun* is read as an active participle, then they are truly those who exceed all bounds in evil, corruption, disbelief, misguidance, and degradation to the utmost degree.

Guidance of the verses:

1- Clarification of the social condition in which the polytheists lived, namely their dislike of daughters out of fear of shame.

2- Clarification of their ignorance of the Lord, the Exalted: they affirm Him but are ignorant of His attributes, to the point that they attributed offspring and partners to Him.

3- Clarification of the reason why wrongdoers are left for a time to persist in wrongdoing, evil, and corruption.

4- Clarification of the wrong belief of those who do not believe in the Hereafter: they ascribe the best reward to themselves, attribute to Allah what they dislike, such as daughters and partners, and revile and degrade the messengers.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 16, verses 63–66:

Explanation of the words:

*Ta-llahi* (by Allah): that is, "wallahi" (by Allah).

*Arsalna ila umamin min qablika* (We sent to nations before you): that is, messengers.

*Fa-zayyana lahumu sh-shaytanu a'malahum* (Then Satan made their deeds seem good to them): so they denied those messengers.

*Fa-huwa waliyyuhumu al-yawma* (So he is their protector today): that is, Satan is their protector, that is, in this world.

*Inna fi dhalika la-ayah* (Indeed, in that is a sign): that is, a clear proof of the soundness of the belief in the Resurrection of the Hereafter.

*La-ayatun li-qawmin yasma'un* (a sign for a people who listen): that is, listening with reflection and understanding.

*La-'ibratan* (indeed a lesson): that is, a strong proof by which one passes from ignorance to knowledge, because *'ibrah* (lesson) comes from *'ubur* (crossing over).

*Min bayni farthin* (from between digestive contents): that is, the *thafal* (contents) of the rumen, meaning the dung found in the rumen.

*Labanan khalisan* (pure milk): that is, free of anything from the dung or the blood, neither its color, nor its smell, nor its taste.

Meaning of the verses:

God Almighty swears by Himself to His Messenger, saying, "By Allah, O Our Messenger, ﴿We have certainly sent﴾ messengers ﴿to nations before you﴾ who were polytheists and disbelievers like your nation, ﴿and Satan made their deeds seem good to them﴾, so they opposed Our messengers, fought them, and persisted in polytheism and disbelief, and so Satan took them as allies. Therefore ﴿he is their protector today﴾, that is, in this world, ﴿and for them is a painful punishment﴾ in the Hereafter." The noble context is one of consoling the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and therefore in the second verse God says: ﴿And We did not send down to you the Book﴾, that is, to burden and torment you, ﴿but that you may make clear to them that over which they differ﴾ concerning monotheism and polytheism, guidance and misguidance. Just as We sent down the Book as ﴿guidance and mercy for a people who believe﴾, by which believers are guided to the paths of their happiness and success, and as mercy that they attain by acting upon it in belief, worship, character, manners and judgment, so that they live compassionately, with brotherhood and love prevailing among them, and mercy and peace enveloping them.

After this consolation of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), the discourse returns to calling to monotheism and the belief in the Resurrection and recompense, after affirming Muhammadan prophethood with His saying: ﴿By Allah, We have certainly sent﴾, the verse, so God says: ﴿And Allah sent down water from the sky and gave life thereby to the earth after its death﴾. The water is rain water, and the life of the earth is by plants and crops after it had been dead, with no vegetation in it. His saying ﴿Indeed, in that﴾, the mentioned sending down of water from the sky and reviving the earth after its death, ﴿is a sign﴾ clear in its indication and decisive of His existence, power, knowledge and mercy, just as it is a sign of resurrection after death, all the more so. And His saying: ﴿And indeed, in the livestock there is a lesson for you﴾, that is, a state by which you pass from ignorance to knowledge... from ignorance of Allah's power and mercy and the obligation to worship Him by remembering and thanking Him, to knowledge of that and recognition of Him, so that you may believe, affirm His unity and obey Him. He explained the aspect of the great lesson, saying: ﴿We give you drink from what is in their bellies﴾, that is, the bellies of the aforementioned livestock, ﴿from between digestive contents and blood, pure milk, palatable to the drinkers﴾. So glory be to Him of wondrous power, vast knowledge and wisdom whose worth cannot be measured. Milk lies between the digestive contents and the blood: the blood passes to the liver, which distributes it through the veins to sustain the animal's life, the milk is conveyed to the udder, and the digestive contents remain at the bottom of the rumen. The milk comes out pure, free from any admixture of blood or of digestive contents, so that neither its color, nor its smell, nor its taste shows any of them, as evidenced by its being palatable to drinkers, so no drinker chokes on it or is strangled by it. Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 16, verses 67–70:

Explanation of the words:

"And of the fruits of the date palms and grapes": that is, among some of the fruits of the date palms and grapes is that from which you take intoxicant (sakar), i.e., wine, "and provision good": i.e., dates, raisins, vinegar and date syrup (dibs) are the good provision.

"And your Lord inspired the bee": i.e., He inspired it to do what it does by an inspiration from Him, exalted is He.

"And of what they build (ya'rishun)": i.e., what they build for it.

"Follow the ways of your Lord, made easy (dhululan)": i.e., the paths of your Lord made smooth, so that travelling them is not difficult for you and you do not go astray from them.

"Drink (sharab)": i.e., honey.

"Wherein is healing for mankind": i.e., from diseases, if it is drunk with the intention of healing, or when combined with another medicine.

"To the most abject age (ardhal al-'umr)": i.e., its lowest and basest, from senility and dementia (kharaf), and kharaf is the corruption of the intellect.

Meaning of the verses:

The context continues to mention the manifestations of God's power, knowledge, wisdom and mercy, which necessitate that He alone be worshipped and which establish the doctrine of prophethood and the final resurrection. God, the Exalted, said, in the course of explaining this, in the style of favour which calls for gratitude: "And of the fruits of the date palms and grapes you take from them intoxicant" and good provision. That is, among some of the fruits of the date palms and grapes is that from which you take intoxicant, i.e., an intoxicating drink. This was before the prohibition of wine. "And good provision" is the raisins and vinegar from grapes, and the dates and date syrup, honey, from the palm. And His saying: "Indeed in that is a sign for a people who reason" means: indeed in what We have mentioned to you is a sign, i.e., a clear proof of Our power, knowledge and mercy, for a people who reason about matters and perceive the outcomes of premises. He who possesses power, knowledge and mercy is the one who deserves to be deified and worshipped.

And His saying: "And your Lord inspired the bee: take for yourself dwellings in the mountains and in the trees and in what they build." This is another great manifestation of God the Exalted's power, knowledge, wisdom and mercy, made manifest by informing the insect, the bee, how it produces honey and offers it to mankind, wherein is a cure for every disease. So His saying "And your Lord inspired" — O Messenger — "the bee," by inspiring it, "take for yourself dwellings in the mountains and in the trees," also as dwellings, "and in what they build for you," i.e., what people build for you, take for yourself dwellings from that, since the bee takes for itself a dwelling inside the trellis that is built for it, which it constructs with the wax it secretes. And His saying, the Exalted: "Then eat of all the fruits," i.e., He inspired it to eat from all the fruits it obtains from the trees and plants, i.e., from their blossoms and flowers. And His saying to it: "So follow the ways of your Lord, made easy," by inspiration from Him, you follow what He has made subservient to you, which are the paths, so you move from one place to another seeking your food, then return to your dwellings, not failing and not going astray, by God's making those paths easy and subservient to it; so you find in them no difficulty and you do not forget them and miss them. And His saying, the Exalted: "There comes forth from their bellies a drink" — i.e., from the bellies of the bees — "its colours vary," i.e., honey which is drunk, varying between white, red and black, or white tinged with red or inclining to yellow. And His saying: "Wherein is healing for mankind": i.e., from ailments. This indefinite form, "healing" (shifa'), indicates that it cures some ailments but not others, which is permissible; this holds unless it is combined with some other medicines or drugs. As for when taken with the intention of healing by a believer, it is a healing for every disease, and without any combination with anything else.

In a sound hadith, in summary, a man complained to the Messenger of God (ﷺ) that his brother's stomach was running, i.e., his belly was loose. He said to him: "Give him honey to drink." He gave him to drink, then he returned and said: "I do not see that it has increased him except in looseness." He returned and he said the same as before, three times, and on the fourth or third time the Messenger of God (ﷺ) said to him: "God has spoken the truth and your brother's belly has lied. Give him the honey to drink." He gave him to drink and he got up as if he had been released from a fetter. And His saying: "Indeed in that" — i.e., the aforementioned inspiration of God to the bee and His teaching it how to make honey, so that there comes forth from its bellies a drink of varying colours wherein is healing for mankind — is a clear proof of God's knowledge, power, mercy and wisdom, which necessitate that He alone be worshipped and deified to the exclusion of others. "But a sign for a people who reflect" upon things, their creation, their causes and their outcomes, so that they are guided to what is required of them, which is that they remember, be admonished, repent to their Creator and submit to Him by worshipping Him alone, to the exclusion of others. And His saying, the Exalted, in the other verse [70]: "And God created you, then He causes you to die, and among you is one who is returned to the most abject age, so that he knows nothing after knowing." This is another verse, more majestic and greater in indicating God's power, knowledge, wisdom and mercy, and it necessitates His worship alone and obliges belief in the final resurrection. God's creation of us, alone, while He is One and we cannot be counted, then His causing us to die a true death, seizing our souls, and no one can avoid dying or ever be exempt from death. Then among the manifestations of wisdom is that He causes us to die at different ages, which wisdom requires for the preservation of the species and the continuation of life to its end. Among people is one who dies as a child, and among them one who dies as a youth, all according to the wisdom of trial and divine upbringing. And another verse: that among us is one who is returned to the basest of his age, i.e., its worst and lowest, so that he becomes senile and demented, losing the strength of body and mind he once had, and no one can deliver him from that except God. It is a manifestation of power and mercy. Have you considered: if God willed to return all people to the most abject age, even within a century or two of years, how would people's lives be then? And His saying: "Indeed God is All-Knowing, All-Powerful" is an affirmation of His knowledge and power, since what He mentioned of our creation, our death, and the return of some of us to the most abject age occurs and exists only by the power of the Powerful and the knowledge of the Knower, who is God, the All-Knowing, the All-Powerful.

Guidance from the verses:

1- Explanation of God's favour upon His servants by mentioning some of their provisions to them, so that they thank God for His blessings.

2- Explanation of God's signs which indicate His power, knowledge and wisdom in the creation of human drink, food and medicine.

3- The virtue of reason, reasoning, thought and reflection.

4- Affirmation of the doctrine of belief in the Last Day, which is indicated by divine power and knowledge, for He who created and caused to die is not thought strange to create again and to cause to die.
