Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 16, verse 71–74:

Explanation of the words:

﴿Fa-faddala ba'dakum 'ala ba'd fi al-rizq﴾ (God has favoured some of you over others in provision): i.e., among you is the rich and among you is the poor, and among you is the owner and among you is the owned.

﴿Fa-hum fihi sawa'﴾ and ﴿Biraddi rizqihim 'ala ma malakat aymanuhum﴾ (Those who would not give their provision to those whom their right hands possess): i.e., by making what We have provided for them a partnership between them and their slaves, the servants they own.

﴿Wallahu ja'ala lakum min anfusikum azwajan﴾ (God made for you mates from yourselves): since Hawwa' was created from Adam and all other women from the drops of men's seed.

﴿Wa hafadah﴾ (and grandchildren/helpers): i.e., servants from one's wife, children, grandchildren, servants, and in-laws.

﴿Afa-bil-batili yu'minun﴾ (Do they then believe in falsehood?): i.e., do they believe in the worship of idols?

﴿Rizqan min al-samawati wa al-ard﴾ (provision from the heavens and the earth): i.e., by sending down rain from the sky and causing plants to grow from the earth.

Meaning of the verses:

The majestic context continues in establishing monotheism and refuting the association of partners with God. God the Exalted says: ﴿And God has favoured some of you over others in provision﴾. Among you, O people, is the one whom He has made wealthy and the one whom He has made poor. Some of you, O wealthy ones, have slaves owned by you. Why are you not content to make your slaves partners in your wealth, so that they would be equal in it, with neither one having an advantage over the other? The answer is that you say, in strange denial, "How could I equate my slave with myself in my provision, so that we become equal? This is unthinkable!" Then how did you permit associating your gods in the worship of your Lord, when they are owned by Him, the Exalted, since He is their Creator and your Creator and the Owner of all of you? Where have your minds gone, O polytheists? And His words: ﴿Do they then deny the favour of God?﴾ Truly, they denied first the blessing of the intellect, so they did not acknowledge it, and therefore they did not reflect with their minds. Then they denied God's favour upon them in their creation and their provision, so they did not worship Him by remembering Him and thanking Him, and they worshipped other than Him, idols and images that possess nothing, harm nothing and benefit nothing. This is what the first verse [71] indicates. As for the second verse, God the Exalted says in it, affirming His blessings upon the polytheists after rebuking them for neglecting their minds in the first verse and for their ingratitude for the blessings of their Lord. He says: ﴿And God﴾, i.e., alone, ﴿has made for you mates from yourselves, and made for you from your mates children and grandchildren, and provided you with good things﴾. That is, He made for you mates from yourselves, human beings of your own kind, with whom you find tranquillity, understand one another and cooperate by the bond of human kinship, and this is a great blessing. He made for you from those mates children through procreation and birth, and also grandchildren (ḥafadah). What is meant by ḥafadah is everyone who hastens (yaḥfid), that is, hurries to serve you and fulfil your needs: your wife, your child, your grandchild, your son-in-law (khatan), i.e., your in-law, and your servant, for all of them hasten to serve you by God's subjugating them to you. Thirdly, ﴿and He provided you with good things﴾, i.e., lawful food and drink, in their variety, diversity of taste, flavour and delight. This is God, whom you are called to worship alone, but you disbelieve. Thus you have come to believe in falsehood, which is the idols and their worship, and to deny the Benefactor and His blessings. Therefore they deserved rebuke and reproach, and God said: ﴿Do they then believe in falsehood and deny the blessing of God?﴾ For their not worshipping the Benefactor, Mighty and Majestic, is itself their ingratitude for the blessing of God the Exalted. And His words ﴿and they worship besides God﴾, i.e., idols that possess for them ﴿no provision from the heavens﴾, by sending down rain, ﴿or the earth﴾, by causing crops and fruits to grow, ﴿not even a little, and they are unable to do anything of that, due to their inherent incapacity, for they are images carved from stone or wood. In this there is, for them, an admonition about their error beyond measure.

And His words: ﴿So do not set up similitudes for God. Indeed, God knows and you do not know﴾. That is, He, the Exalted, forbids them from making likenesses for God by taking idols as gods, applying the word "god" to them, whereas God has no likeness; and by believing that they intercede for them with God and bring them near to Him, and that they are an intermediary like a minister to a ruler, and so on. He forbade them from setting up these similitudes for God the Exalted because He, Mighty and Majestic, knows that He has no likeness and no equal; rather He is the One, there is no god but He, exalted above the similar, the equal and the peer. But they do not know, and therefore they are bewildered and stumbling in the darkness of polytheism and the valleys of error.

The guidance of the verses:

From the guidance of the verses:

1- Cutting off the root of polytheism in the parable contained in the first verse: ﴿And God has favoured some of you over others in provision﴾.

2- The obligation to thank God for His blessings, by remembering Him, thanking Him and sincerely devoting that to Him.

3- The ugliness of ingratitude for blessings and of ignoring the Benefactor by not thanking Him for them.

4- Condemnation of those who set up similitudes for God while they do not know, by adopting intermediaries for Him, likening God to His servants; they seek intercession through the saints and prophets, calling upon them and seeking their aid, as those brought near to God who are answered by Him, and who answer no one else.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 16, verses 75–78:

Explanation of the words:

"Allah sets forth an example": that is, a slave owned (by another), etc.

"A slave owned": that is, not free, but a slave owned by someone else.

"Are they equal?": that is, the helpless slaves and the free person who disposes of his own affairs. The answer: they are certainly not equal.

"And Allah sets forth an example": that is, two men, etc.

"Dumb (abkam)": that is, a child who is mute and deaf, who does not hear.

"Has no power over anything": that is, he cannot understand, nor make others understand.

"And to Allah belongs the unseen of the heavens and the earth": that is, whatever is hidden in them.

"And the matter of the Hour": that is, the matter of its establishment, which is by causing the living to die and bringing them back to life, together with those who died before, and by changing the forms of all existence.

"Hearts (af'idah)": that is, the hearts.

Meaning of the verses:

The context still concerns establishing monotheism, calling to it, refuting polytheism and warning against it. It has already been mentioned that Allah the Exalted rebukes the polytheists for setting forth examples for Him, while He has no like and no equal. In this context, Allah, who is All-Knowing and All-Aware, sets forth two examples. The first, He says: ﴿Allah sets forth an example: a slave owned (by another)﴾, that is, not a free person among men, ﴿who has no power over anything﴾, since he is owned and has no right to dispose of his master's property except with his permission; therefore he has no power to give or withhold anything. This is one side of the example. The second is ﴿and one whom We have provided with good provision from Us﴾, abundant and good, ﴿so he spends from it secretly and openly﴾, by night and by day, because he is free to dispose of it as its owner. ﴿Are they equal?﴾ The answer: the two are not equal... Therefore ﴿Praise be to Allah! But most of them do not know﴾. The example is struck for both the believer and the disbeliever. The disbeliever is a captive of idols and a slave to them; he recognizes no good and denounces no evil; he does not act in the way of Allah and does not spend, because he does not believe in the Last Abode and its recompense. The believer, however, is free; he acts by the power of Allah, spends in the way of Allah secretly and openly, seeking the Hereafter and reward from Allah, possessing knowledge and will, fearing none but Allah and hoping for nothing but Him, glory be to Him and exalted is He.

His saying ﴿And Allah sets forth an example: two men﴾ is the second example in this context, which is contained in the second verse [76]. He, the Exalted, says in it: ﴿And Allah sets forth an example﴾, which is ﴿two men, one of whom is dumb﴾. The word "dumb" may also indicate deafness, for usually a dumb person does not hear. ﴿He has no power over anything﴾, so he cannot understand others because he is deaf, and others cannot be made to understand him because he is dumb. ﴿And he is a burden on his master﴾, that is, his cousin or whoever among his relatives takes charge of him, who provide for his maintenance and care because of his weakness, impotence and inability to do anything. His saying: ﴿Wherever he directs him, he brings no good﴾, that is, wherever his master and cousin direct him to bring something, he brings no good; he may bring evil, but as for benefit and good, nothing comes from him.

This is the likeness of the idols that are worshipped besides Allah, for they neither hear nor see, so they do not understand what is said to them, nor do they make their worshippers understand anything, and they are in need of them in their making, placement, carrying and protection.

His, the Exalted's, saying: ﴿Is he equal to one who enjoins justice and is on a straight path?﴾ refers to Allah, the Exalted, who enjoins justice, that is, monotheism and uprightness in everything; He is the Sustainer of everything, and He is upon a straight path, calling people to follow it so that they may be saved and made happy in both abodes. The answer: the two are by no means equal. How, then, do the polytheists accept the worship and guardianship of the dumb one who has no power over anything, and abandon the worship of the All-Hearing, All-Seeing, the Strong, the Powerful, who calls them to their perfection and happiness in both their lives? This is a matter that causes wonder, but there is no wonder with the decrees of Allah and the arrangements of the All-Wise, All-Knowing.

His, the Exalted's, saying in verse [77]: ﴿And to Allah belongs the unseen of the heavens and the earth﴾: He alone knows what is hidden from us in them. He knows who has been decreed happiness and who has been condemned to wretchedness, who is guided and who is not guided; the recompense comes with the coming of the Hour. ﴿And the matter of the Hour is but as a glance of the eye or even nearer﴾, that is, its coming, ﴿for it requires only a word: "Be," and it is﴾, its matter depending only upon the word "Be", so that this life ends with all that is in it, and the other life comes, the forms of all things having been changed. ﴿Indeed, Allah is over all things Competent﴾, and among that is the establishment of the Resurrection and the coming of the Hour. His, the Exalted's, saying: ﴿And Allah brought you forth from the wombs of your mothers, knowing nothing﴾: a fact that cannot be denied. Allah is the One who brought us forth from the wombs of our mothers after He had shaped us in the wombs and nourished us until we became human, then He permitted our emergence; we emerged, knowing nothing at all. This is a sign of divine power, divine knowledge and divine arrangement. Does anything of this belong to the idols? The answer is no. Secondly, Allah the Exalted made for us hearing, sight and hearts (af'idah) as another blessing, for had it not been so, we would not have heard, seen or reasoned, and what would be the worth of our life on that day, since non-existence would be better than it? His saying: ﴿So that you may give thanks﴾ is a complete disclosure of the secret of this blessing: He made us hear, see and reason so that He might obligate us, commanding us and forbidding us, and we obey Him by complying with His commands and avoiding His prohibitions. That is our thanks to Him, along with the good that is in such thanks. It is preparation for happiness in both abodes. So is there anyone who takes heed, O servants of Allah?!

Guidance of the verses:

From the guidance of these verses:

1- The commendability of setting forth examples, which is comparing one state with another, on condition that the one who sets forth the example is knowing.

2- Clarification of the example of the believer in his perfection and of the disbeliever in his deficiency.

3- Clarification of the example of the idols in their lifelessness, the toil of their worshippers over them in protecting them, and their not benefiting from them; and the example of the Lord, blessed and exalted, in His justice, His call to Islam and His standing upon it, together with His answering the supplication of His friends, His care for them, His knowledge of them, His hearing of their supplication, His support of them in their lives, His honoring them, and His bestowing favours upon them in both their lives. And to Allah belongs the highest example, and He is the Mighty, the Wise.

"A slave owned": that is, not free, but a slave owned by someone else.

"And Allah sets forth an example": that is, two men, etc.

"Dumb (abkam)": that is, a child who is mute and deaf, who does not hear.

"Has no power over anything": that is, he cannot understand, nor make others understand.

"And to Allah belongs the unseen of the heavens and the earth": that is, whatever is hidden in them.

"And the matter of the Hour": that is, the matter of its establishment, which is by causing the living to die and bringing them back to life, together with those who died before, and by changing the forms of all existence.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 16, verses 79–83:

Explanation of the words:

*Musakhkharat fi jaww al-sama'* (subjected in the air of the sky): i.e., made subservient in the expanse between the sky and the earth, which is the air.

*Ma yumsikuhunna* (none holds them up): i.e., when they fold and spread their wings, *illa Allah* (except God) by His power and His laws in His creation.

*Min buyutikum sakanan* (of your houses a dwelling): i.e., a place in which you dwell and settle for rest.

*Min juluud al-an'am buyutan* (from the hides of livestock, houses): i.e., tents and domes.

*Yawm az-ta'nikum* (the day of your travelling): i.e., your departure on your journeys.

*Athathan wa mata'an ila hin* (furnishings and provision for a time): such as rugs and coverings, which wear out, tear, and are discarded.

*Zilalan wa min al-jibal aknanan* (shade, and from the mountains, shelters): i.e., what you shelter under from the heat of the sun, and what you dwell in within the caves of the mountains.

*Wa sarabil* (and garments): i.e., shirts that protect you from heat and cold.

*Wa sarabil taqikum ba'sakum* (and garments that protect you from your violence): i.e., coats of mail that protect you from blows and spear-thrusts in war.

*La'allakum tuslimun* (that perhaps you may submit): i.e., in hope that you submit your hearts and faces to Him, so that you worship Him alone.

Meaning of the verses:

The noble context continues to establish monotheism, call to it, and refute and abandon polytheism. He, exalted, says: ﴿Have they not considered the birds, subjected in the air of the sky? None holds them up except Allah﴾. Indeed, in the creation of birds of various kinds and their great numbers, and in their flight in the expanse of the sky, i.e., in the air, and how they fold their wings and spread them, and do not fall to the earth, who holds them but God, by whatever He wills of His management in His creation and His universe? Indeed, in what has been mentioned are many signs that point to the Creator, His power and His knowledge, and that require knowing Him, drawing near to Him, and obeying Him by worshipping Him alone, as they also point to the falsehood of deifying other than Him and worshipping anything besides Him. That these signs are for a people who believe is in terms of their being people with living hearts, who perceive and understand, unlike the disbelievers, who have dead hearts, so there is no perception or understanding for them, and thus there is no sign in this for them.

And His saying: ﴿And Allah has made for you from your houses a dwelling﴾, i.e., a place of settling and rest. ﴿And He has made for you from the hides of livestock﴾, camels, cattle, and sheep, ﴿houses﴾, i.e., tents and domes, ﴿which you find light to carry﴾, i.e., you find them light in transport, ﴿on the day of your travelling﴾, i.e., your departure on your journeys and your moves, ﴿and on the day of your residing﴾ in one place likewise. And His saying: ﴿And from their wool, their fur, and their hair﴾, i.e., He made for you from them ﴿furnishings﴾ such as rugs, carpets, and coverings, ﴿and provision﴾, i.e., you enjoy them for a time until they wear out and tear. And His saying: ﴿And Allah has made for you, from what He created﴾ of many things, ﴿shades﴾ by which you shelter from the heat of the sun, ﴿and has made for you from the mountains refuges﴾ in which you shelter yourselves from rain, cold, or heat, and they are caves and grottoes in the mountains. ﴿And has made for you garments﴾, shirts, ﴿that protect you from the heat﴾ and the cold, ﴿and garments﴾, which are coats of mail, ﴿that protect you from your violence﴾ in war, by which you guard against sword-blows and spear-thrusts. Is not He who made for you all these things more deserving of your worship and obedience? And thus ﴿He completes His favour upon you﴾, so He sent to you His Messenger and sent down to you His Book, to prepare you for Islam so that you may submit. Here, and after this clear explanation and eloquent reminder, He says to His Messenger: ﴿But if they turn away﴾, i.e., they turn away from what you have reminded them of, so do not grieve or regret, for it is not upon you to guide them: ﴿Your duty is only to convey the clear message﴾, and you have conveyed and made clear. So there is no further responsibility or accountability upon you. And His saying: ﴿They recognise the favour of Allah﴾, i.e., the favour of Allah upon them, as we have reminded them of it, ﴿then they deny it﴾, so they worship other than the Bestower of it, ﴿and most of them are disbelievers﴾, i.e., those who deny and reject your prophethood and your message and the Islam you have brought.

Guidance of the verses:

From the guidance of the verses:

1- Only believers benefit from the signs, because their hearts are alive; as for the disbelievers, they are in the darkness of disbelief, seeing nothing of the signs and not perceiving.

2- The manifestations of God's power, knowledge, wisdom, mercy and blessings appear in these four verses, and it is strange that the polytheists, like the disbelievers, are blind and see nothing of them, and most of them are disbelievers.

3- The duty of the Messenger ﷺ is not to guide hearts but to explain the way through clear conveyance.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 16, verses 84–89:

Explanation of the words:

﻿"And [mention] the Day We raise up from every nation a witness": i.e., mention the day We raise up.

"A witness": he is their prophet.

"They will not be permitted [to present excuses] to those who disbelieved": i.e., to offer excuses, so that they might make their excuses.

"Nor will they be asked to make amends": i.e., they will not be asked to make amends (al-'utba), meaning to return to a belief, speech and action that pleases Allah.

"And when those who associated others with Allah see their partners": i.e., those they used to worship besides Allah, such as idols and devils.

"Then they will cast to them the word": i.e., they will answer them, saying to them, "Indeed, you are liars."

"And they will submit to Allah that Day": i.e., they will humble themselves to Him, submit to His judgment, and surrender.

"And lost from them is what they used to invent": regarding their claim that their gods would intercede for them with Allah and save them from His punishment. The word "lost" (ḍalla) means "disappeared."

"A punishment over and above the punishment": that it is scorpions and serpents, like tall palm trees and branded mules.

"And We have sent down to you the Book": i.e., the Qur'an.

"As an clarification for all things": i.e., for everything the nation needs in knowing the lawful and the unlawful, the truth and falsehood, reward and punishment.

Meaning of the verses:

The noble context of these six verses is concentrated on affirming the Resurrection and recompense together with prophethood. His saying, Exalted is He, "﴿And [mention] the Day We raise up from every nation﴾," i.e., mention, O Our Messenger Muhammad, the day We raise up from every nation among the nations "﴿a witness﴾," who is their prophet, who was sent among them and to them. "﴿Then He will not permit those who disbelieved﴾," i.e., to make excuses, "﴿so they will make excuses﴾," "﴿nor will they be asked to make amends﴾," i.e., they will not be asked to make amends, meaning to return to a belief, speech and action that pleases Allah concerning them. Mention this to your people, perhaps they will remember, be admonished, repent, be saved and be happy. His saying in the second verse [85], "﴿And when those who did wrong see the punishment﴾," i.e., on the Day of Resurrection, "﴿its punishment will not be lightened for them, nor will they be given respite﴾," i.e., they will not be granted time. Mention this too, as a reminder and instruction, and mention to them: "﴿And when those who associated others [with Allah] see their partners﴾" in the plains of Resurrection or in Hell, they will cry out, saying "﴿Our Lord﴾," i.e., O our Lord, "﴿these are our partners whom we used to call upon besides You﴾," i.e., we used to worship them by calling upon them and seeking their help, "﴿then they will cast to them the word﴾" immediately, "﴿Indeed, you are liars﴾." "﴿And they will submit to Allah that Day﴾," i.e., submission, so they will humble themselves to His judgment. "﴿And lost from them is what they used to invent﴾" in the world of falsehoods and fabrications, such as their saying, "These are our intercessors with Allah," and that they will be saved from the Fire through their intercession, and that they are their means to Allah. All of that "﴿was lost﴾," i.e., it disappeared from them, and they found nothing of it. His saying, Exalted is He: "﴿Those who disbelieved and barred from the way of Allah﴾," who turned others away by calling them to disbelief and its causes, and at times compelled them to it through intimidation and enticement, "﴿We will increase them in punishment upon punishment﴾" which they deserved by their disbelief. It is related that this increase in punishment is scorpions like black mules, and serpents like tall palm trees, and we seek refuge with Allah, Exalted is He, from the Fire and the various kinds of torment within it. His saying, Exalted is He: "﴿And [mention] the Day We raise up﴾," i.e., mention, O Our Messenger, the day We raise up "﴿in every nation a witness against them from among themselves﴾," i.e., on the Day of Resurrection, "﴿and We will bring you as a witness against these [people]﴾," i.e., against those to whom you were sent from your nation.

How will the situation be when you bear witness against the people of faith for their faith, against the people of disbelief for their disbelief, against the people of monotheism for their monotheism, and against the people of polytheism for their polytheism? Indeed, it is a difficult situation in which regret is great and remorse intense. His saying, Exalted is He, addressing His Messenger, affirming his prophethood and the revelation to him: "﴿And We have sent down to you the Book﴾," i.e., the Qur'an, "﴿as clarification for all things﴾" that the nation needs to know, of the lawful and unlawful, rulings, and proofs, "﴿and guidance﴾" from all misguidance, "﴿and mercy﴾" especially for those who act upon it and apply it to themselves and their lives, so it is a general mercy among them, "﴿and glad tidings for the Muslims﴾," i.e., those who submit to Allah in His commands and prohibitions, glad tidings for them of great reward and abundant recompense on the Day of Resurrection, and of victory, success and honor in this world. After Our sending down this Book to you, no excuse remains for anyone who wishes to make excuses on the Day of Resurrection. Therefore your testimony over your nation will be the greatest testimony and the most influential in the salvation of those who are saved and the destruction of those who are destroyed, and none is destroyed before Allah except one who is destined to destruction.

Guidance from the verses:

1- Affirmation of the belief in the Last Resurrection in a manner that cannot be exceeded, given the many varieties of presentation of what takes place on that Day.

2- The disassociation of the devils and idols that people associated with Allah in worship, and their disavowal of those who associated them, and their denial.

3- Increased punishment for whoever calls to polytheism and disbelief and drives people toward it.

4- No excuse remains for anyone after Allah has sent down the Qur'an as clarification for all things, and as guidance, mercy and glad tidings for the Muslims.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 16, verses 90–93:

Explanation of the words:

al-'Adl (justice): equity, and from it comes tawhid (affirmation of God's oneness).

al-Ihsan (excellence): performing the obligatory duties and abstaining from what is forbidden, while remaining mindful of God, may He be exalted.

Wa-ita'i dhi al-qurba (and giving to the near of kin): that is, giving the near of kin their rights of kinship and goodness.

'An al-fahsha' (from indecency): fornication (zina).

Ya'izukum (He admonishes you): that is, He commands you and forbids you.

Tadhakkarun (you may be mindful): that is, you may take heed.

Tawkidiha (their confirmation): that is, their strengthening.

Naqadat ghazlaha (unravelled her yarn): that is, she ruined her yarn after spinning it.

Min ba'di quwwatin (after strength): that is, after it had been made firm and twisted.

Ankathan (into pieces): plural of nakth, which is that which is unravelled and undone after being twisted.

Ka-allati naqadat ghazlaha (like the one who unravelled her yarn): she was a foolish woman of Makkah, called Rayta bint Sa'd ibn Taym al-Qurashiyya.

Dakhalan baynakum (as a means of deceit among you): al-dakhal is that which enters into a thing while not being part of it, for the purpose of corruption and deception.

Arba min ummah (more numerous than a community): that is, greater than it in number and strength.

Meaning of the verses:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Indeed, Allah commands justice﴾, meaning that Allah commands, in the Book He revealed as an explanation of all things, justice, which is equity. Among this is that He be worshipped by remembering Him and giving Him thanks, because He is the Creator, the Bestower of favours, and that the worship of other than Him be abandoned, because other than Him did not create, did not provide, and did not bestow any favour. Therefore this term was interpreted as "There is no god but Allah." ﴿And excellence﴾, which is performing the obligatory duties and avoiding the forbidden acts, while being mindful of Allah in that, so that performance is in the required manner, with perfection and quality, and avoidance is out of fear of Allah and shame before Him. His saying ﴿and giving to the near of kin﴾, meaning giving those of kinship their rights of goodness and kinship. This is among what Allah, may He be exalted, has commanded in His Book. And among what He forbids is indecency (fahsha'), which is fornication, sodomy, and every ugly act whose ugliness is intense and gross, even stinginess. ﴿And wrongdoing﴾, which is everything the Law denies and that sound natures and upright, sound intellects deny. He forbids transgression (baghy), which is injustice, aggression, and exceeding the limit in all matters. His saying ﴿that you may be mindful﴾, meaning He commanded this in His Book in hope that you would remember and take heed, so that you comply with the command and avoid the prohibition. Thereby you will be perfected and attain happiness. For this reason it has been reported that this verse, ﴿Indeed, Allah commands justice and excellence﴾ up to ﴿you may be mindful﴾, is the most comprehensive verse in the Book of Allah concerning good and evil. And it is so: there is no good except that it has commanded it, and no evil except that it has forbidden it.

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And fulfil the covenant of Allah when you have entered into it﴾, a command from Allah, exalted is He, to the believing servants to fulfil covenants. So every believer who has pledged allegiance to an imam, or made a covenant with someone regarding something, must keep the covenant with him and not diminish it, "for there is no faith for one who has no trustworthiness, and no religion for one who has no covenant," as in the noble hadith.

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And do not break your oaths after their confirmation﴾. Oaths (al-aymān) is the plural of yamin, which is swearing by Allah. Their confirmation is their strengthening through added words. ﴿And you have made Allah your surety (kafil)﴾, meaning your guarantor (wakil); that is, during your swearing by Him, exalted is He, you have made Him your guarantor. This verse prohibits breaking oaths, which is violating them and not adhering to them by breaking them for material interests. His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Indeed, Allah knows what you do﴾ contains a severe warning to whoever breaks his oaths after their confirmation.

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And do not be like her who unravelled her yarn﴾, referring to a foolish woman in Makkah who would spin and then unravel and ruin her yarn after it had been made firm and secure. Allah, exalted is He, forbade the believers to break their oaths after their confirmation, so that their state would be like the state of this foolish woman. His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Taking your oaths as a means of deceit among you﴾, meaning corruption and deception, such as when you enter into an alliance with a group and pledge to them, then you break your covenant and undo what you have firmly agreed as a pact and compact, and make a covenant with another group because it is stronger and you benefit from it more. This is the meaning of His saying ﴿that one community may be more numerous than another community﴾, meaning a group greater than another group in men, weapons, wealth, or advantages. His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Allah only tests you thereby﴾, meaning He tries you, so that these situations present themselves to you and you find yourselves inclined toward them; then you remember your Lord's prohibition against breaking oaths and covenants, and so you abandon that in obedience to your Lord, or you do not, preferring the world over the Hereafter. ﴿And He will surely make clear to you on the Day of Resurrection that wherein you used to differ﴾, then He will judge between you and recompense you, the doer of good for his good and the doer of evil for his evil.

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And if Allah had willed, He would have made you one nation﴾, upon monotheism and guidance, He would have done so. However, His lofty wisdom required that He guide whom He wills to guidance, because he desires it and seeks it, and lead astray whom He wills to be led astray, because he desires misguidance, seeks it, and persists in it after being forbidden. His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And you will surely be questioned about what you used to do﴾, meaning a questioning of rebuke and reproach, ﴿concerning what you used to do﴾ of evil and falsehood. The necessary consequence of this is just recompense: whoever comes with a good deed will have ten times its like, and whoever comes with an evil deed will not be recompensed except with its like, and they will not be wronged.

Guidance from the verses:

1- Clarification of the most comprehensive verse concerning good and evil in the Qur'an, which is the verse ﴿Indeed, Allah commands justice and excellence...﴾ [90].

2- The obligation of justice and excellence, and giving the near of kin their obligatory rights of goodness and kinship.

3- The prohibition of fornication, sodomy, and every ugly act whose ugliness is intense, among the outward and inward indecencies.

4- The prohibition of transgression (baghy), which is injustice in all its forms and shapes.

5- The obligation of fulfilling covenants and the gravity of breaking them.

6- The prohibition of breaking oaths after their confirmation, and training the soul to abide by them, so as to exclude the idle oath (laghw al-yamin).

7- Whoever pledges allegiance to a leader or makes a covenant with anyone is obligated to fulfil it, and breaking or undoing it for worldly benefits is never permissible.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 16, verses 94–97:

Explanation of the words:

*Dakhalan baynakum* (a means of deception between you): i.e., for the purpose of corruption and deceit.

*Wa-tadhuqu as-su'* (and taste the evil): i.e., the punishment.

*Ma 'indakum yanfad* (what is with you will run out): it will perish and come to an end.

*Wa-huwa mu'min* (while he is a believer): i.e., and the state in which, when he did righteous deeds, he was a believer, for without faith no deed is accepted.

*Hayatan tayyibah* (a good life): in this world, through contentment, lawful provision, and in the Hereafter it is the life of Paradise.

*Bi-ahsani ma kanu ya'malun* (according to the best of what they used to do): i.e., He will reward them for all their deeds, both the good and the best of them, according to the best in them.

Meaning of the verses:

The discourse continues on the upbringing of the believers, the people of the Qur'an, which is an exposition of everything, a guidance, a mercy, and good tidings for Muslims. Allah the Exalted says: ﴿And do not take your oaths as means of deception among yourselves﴾, i.e., deceit, ﴿lest a foot slip after it was firmly planted﴾, meaning that one of you falls into a major sin of this kind: he swears by Allah with the intent of deception and misleading, so that you taste evil in this world because of your turning others away from the way of Allah, those with whom you make covenants or pacts and to whom you give your oaths and pledges, and then you break them. These people turn away from Islam and avoid it because of the breaking and reneging they saw from you. You bear the burden of that, and there will be for you a great punishment on the Day of Resurrection. So beware of falling into such a predicament; be careful that a foot of any of you does not slip away from Islam after it has become firmly established in it. As for His saying: ﴿And do not trade the covenant of Allah for a small price﴾, everything in this world is small. And His saying, the Exalted: ﴿What is with Allah is better for you, if you only knew﴾, for what you have of wealth or goods will run out, i.e., perish, ﴿while what is with Allah remains﴾, having no end. So remember this, and do not sell the precious for the cheap, or the lasting for the perishing. And His saying, the Exalted: ﴿And We will surely reward those who were patient﴾ in keeping their covenants, ﴿their reward﴾ for their patience, ﴿according to the best of what they used to do﴾, i.e., their reward is multiplied, and He gives them all their deeds, both the good and the best of them, according to their most excellent and most perfect form, so that the reward of a supererogatory act is like the reward of an obligatory one. This is a promise from Allah the Exalted to whoever is patient in his faith and Islam and does not sell his religion for a small worldly gain. A second promise is in His saying: ﴿Whoever does righteousness, whether male or female, while he is a believer – We will surely cause him to live a good life, and We will surely reward them according to the best of what they used to do﴾. Yet the people of this promise are the people of faith and righteous deeds, true faith that leads to righteous deeds; and it follows that they have abandoned shirk and sins. Their Lord has promised them that He will give them a good life in this world, a life free of impurity, with contentment, good food and drink, and satisfaction. This is in this world, and in the Hereafter, Paradise. The reward will be according to the best deed they performed of each kind: for prayer, according to the best prayer; for charity, according to the best charity; and so on. ﴿And We will surely reward them their reward according to the best of what they used to do﴾. O Allah, make us among them, gather us in their company, and grant us what You promised them, for You are Most Kind and Most Merciful.

Guidance from the verses:

1- The prohibition of taking oaths as a means to cheating, deceit and corruption.

2- What is with Allah is better than what a person obtains by disobeying the Most Merciful of worldly trash.

3- The great reward of patience in obeying Allah the Exalted, in doing and in abstaining.

4- The true promise for whoever believes and does righteousness, male or female: a good life in this world and the Hereafter.

*Wa-tadhuqu as-su'* (and taste the evil): i.e., the punishment.

*Ma 'indakum yanfad* (what is with you will run out): it will perish and come to an end.

*Wa-huwa mu'min* (while he is a believer): i.e., and the state in which, when he did righteous deeds, he was a believer, for without faith no deed is accepted.

*Hayatan tayyibah* (a good life): in this world, through contentment, lawful provision, and in the Hereafter it is the life of Paradise.

*Bi-ahsani ma kanu ya'malun* (according to the best of what they used to do): i.e., He will reward them for all their deeds, both the good and the best of them, according to the best in them.

Meaning of the verses:

The discourse continues on the upbringing of the believers, the people of the Qur'an, which is an exposition of everything, a guidance, a mercy, and good tidings for Muslims. Allah the Exalted says: ﴿And do not take your oaths as means of deception among yourselves﴾, i.e., deceit, ﴿lest a foot slip after it was firmly planted﴾, meaning that one of you falls into a major sin of this kind: he swears by Allah with the intent of deception and misleading, so that you taste evil in this world because of your turning others away from the way of Allah, those with whom you make covenants or pacts and to whom you give your oaths and pledges, and then you break them. These people turn away from Islam and avoid it because of the breaking and reneging they saw from you. You bear the burden of that, and there will be for you a great punishment on the Day of Resurrection. So beware of falling into such a predicament; be careful that a foot of any of you does not slip away from Islam after it has become firmly established in it. As for His saying: ﴿And do not trade the covenant of Allah for a small price﴾, everything in this world is small. And His saying, the Exalted: ﴿What is with Allah is better for you, if you only knew﴾, for what you have of wealth or goods will run out, i.e., perish, ﴿while what is with Allah remains﴾, having no end. So remember this, and do not sell the precious for the cheap, or the lasting for the perishing. And His saying, the Exalted: ﴿And We will surely reward those who were patient﴾ in keeping their covenants, ﴿their reward﴾ for their patience, ﴿according to the best of what they used to do﴾, i.e., their reward is multiplied, and He gives them all their deeds, both the good and the best of them, according to their most excellent and most perfect form, so that the reward of a supererogatory act is like the reward of an obligatory one. This is a promise from Allah the Exalted to whoever is patient in his faith and Islam and does not sell his religion for a small worldly gain. A second promise is in His saying: ﴿Whoever does righteousness, whether male or female, while he is a believer – We will surely cause him to live a good life, and We will surely reward them according to the best of what they used to do﴾. Yet the people of this promise are the people of faith and righteous deeds, true faith that leads to righteous deeds; and it follows that they have abandoned shirk and sins. Their Lord has promised them that He will give them a good life in this world, a life free of impurity, with contentment, good food and drink, and satisfaction. This is in this world, and in the Hereafter, Paradise. The reward will be according to the best deed they performed of each kind: for prayer, according to the best prayer; for charity, according to the best charity; and so on. ﴿And We will surely reward them their reward according to the best of what they used to do﴾. O Allah, make us among them, gather us in their company, and grant us what You promised them, for You are Most Kind and Most Merciful.

Guidance from the verses:

1- The prohibition of taking oaths as a means to cheating, deceit and corruption.

2- What is with Allah is better than what a person obtains by disobeying the Most Merciful of worldly trash.

3- The great reward of patience in obeying Allah the Exalted, in doing and in abstaining.

4- The true promise for whoever believes and does righteousness, male or female: a good life in this world and the Hereafter.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 16, verses 98–102:

Explanation of the words:

"فإذا قرأت القرآن" (So when you recite the Qur'an): i.e., when you intend to recite the Qur'an.

"فاستعذ بالله من الشيطان" (then seek refuge in Allah from Satan): i.e., say, "I seek refuge in Allah from the accursed Satan," to protect yourself from his whisperings.

"إنه ليس له سلطان" (Indeed, he has no authority): i.e., no power or dominion to corrupt and lead astray those who believe, so long as they rely upon Allah.

"وإذا بدلنا آية مكان آية" (And when We substitute one verse in place of another): i.e., by abrogating it and revealing another verse in its place, for the benefit of the servants.

"قل نزله روح القدس" (Say: "The Holy Spirit has brought it down"): i.e., Jibril (peace be upon him).

"ليثبت الذين آمنوا" (to strengthen those who believe): i.e., in their faith.

Meaning of the verses:

The noble context continues with the guidance and perfecting of the Muslims. As for His saying, Exalted is He, "﴿So when you recite the Qur'an﴾" O Muhammad, you or any of the believers who follow you, "﴿seek refuge in Allah from Satan, the accursed﴾", i.e., if you are a reciter resolved to recite, then say, "I seek refuge in Allah from the accursed Satan," for that protects you from his whisperings, which may corrupt your recitation. And His saying, "﴿Indeed, he has no authority﴾", i.e., Satan has no authority, meaning domination, dominance and subjugation, "﴿over those who believe and rely upon their Lord﴾", and this is a glad tiding of good for the believers. "﴿His authority is only over those who take him as an ally﴾" by obeying him and acting upon his adornment of evil and falsehood, "﴿and those who associate others with Him﴾". These are the ones over whom Satan has dominion, so he misguides and leads them astray until he destroys them. And His saying, Exalted is He, "﴿And when We substitute one verse in place of another﴾", i.e., We abrogate one ruling by another ruling through a different verse. The polytheists who denied the divine revelation said, "﴿You, [O Muhammad], are only a fabricator﴾", speaking falsely and by conjecture, i.e., one says something today and its opposite tomorrow. And His saying, Exalted is He, "﴿And Allah is most knowing of what He sends down﴾", for He sends it down for the benefit of His servants, abrogating and confirming for the sake of the interests of the believers. Allah, Exalted is He, taught His Messenger how to respond to this doubt, saying to him, "﴿Say: The Pure Spirit has brought it down from your Lord in truth﴾". So it is not you who says what you wish; rather, it is the revelation and speech of Allah, brought down by Jibril (peace be upon him) from your Lord in truth, the established truth with Allah that neither changes nor alters. This is for the benefit of strengthening those who believe in their faith and submission. Thus, whenever a Qur'an is revealed, the believers increase in faith. It is like rain that falls upon the earth: whenever it falls, the earth's life increases in freshness and delight; likewise, the descent of the Qur'an gives life to the hearts of the believers. And it, the Qur'an, is guidance from every misguidance, and a glad tiding for all Muslims of success in this world and triumph in the Hereafter.

Guidance of the verses:

From the guidance of the verses:

1- The recommendation of seeking refuge when reciting the Qur'an with the words: "I seek refuge in Allah from the accursed Satan."

2- Clarification that Satan has no dominion over believers who rely upon their Lord.

3- Clarification that Satan's authority is over his allies who obey him and associate others with their Lord.

4- Clarification that the Qur'an contains the abrogating and the abrogated (al-nasikh wa'l-mansukh, abrogation in the Qur'an).

5- Clarification of the benefit of the Qur'an's descent with abrogation and its confirmation, which is to strengthen those who believe in their faith, guidance from misguidance, and a glad tiding to Muslims of success and triumph in both abodes.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 16, verses 103–109:

Explanation of the words:

Bashar (a human being): they mean a Christian smith (blacksmith) in Makkah.

Lisan alladhi yulhiduna ilayhi (the tongue of the one they incline towards): i.e., they incline towards it.

Wa hadha lisanun 'arabiyyun (and this is a clear Arabic tongue): i.e., the Qur'an, so how could a non-Arab (a'jami) teach it?

Illa man ukriha (except one who is compelled): i.e., compelled to utter disbelief, and he uttered it.

Wa lakin man shara bil-kufri sadran (but whoever opens his breast to disbelief): i.e., he opened his breast to disbelief and expanded it for it, so that his soul was content with it.

Wa ulaika hum al-ghafilun (and those are the heedless): i.e., heedless of what is intended for them.

La jaram (undoubtedly): i.e., truly.

Hum al-khasirun (they are the losers): i.e., because their destiny is the Fire, abiding therein forever.

Explanation of the verses:

The noble context continues in refuting the polytheists who accused the Messenger ﷺ of fabrication, so the Exalted says: ﴿And We know that they say, "It is only a human being who teaches him."﴾ That is, a person of mankind teaches Muhammad, not that it is revelation he receives from Allah. The Exalted said, refuting this slander and nullifying it: ﴿The tongue of the one they incline towards﴾ i.e., they incline towards him, claiming that he is the one who teaches Muhammad, ﴿is non-Arabic⁠﻿﻿﻿﻿﻿﻿—﻿﻿﻿—⁠ and he is a Roman slave. ﴿And this﴾ i.e., the Qur'an, ﴿is a clear Arabic tongue﴾, possessing eloquence, rhetoric and clarity. How, then, does this agree with what they say, that they are merely lying? And His saying ﴿Indeed, those who do not believe in the signs of Allah﴾, which are light, guidance, decisive proofs and a shining demonstration, ﴿Allah does not guide them﴾ to knowledge of the truth and the path of rectitude, because they turned away from the way of guidance and barred themselves from the path of recognition. And His saying ﴿and for them is a painful punishment﴾, i.e., the recompense for their disbelief in the signs of Allah. And His saying ﴿It is only those who do not believe in the signs of Allah who invent falsehood, and they are the liars﴾, i.e., it is only the disbeliever in the signs of Allah who fabricates falsehood and actually lies, because he does not hope for Allah's reward nor fear His punishment; therefore nothing restrains him from lying. As for the believer, he hopes for the reward of truthfulness and fears the punishment of lying, so he never lies. Thus it is established that the Prophet did not invent falsehood; rather, it is those deniers of the signs of Allah who invent falsehood, and they are truly the liars. And His Exalted saying: ﴿Whoever disbelieves in Allah after his faith, except one who is compelled﴾ to utter disbelief ﴿while his heart is at rest with faith﴾, not harbouring any doubt, nor finding any agitation or anxiety, and he says the word of disbelief only with his tongue. Such is the case of 'Ammar ibn Yasir, whom the Quraysh compelled to utter the word of disbelief, so the Messenger ﷺ permitted him to say it with his tongue. ﴿But whoever opens his breast to disbelief﴾, i.e., is content with disbelief and his soul is at ease with it, ﴿upon them is wrath from Allah, and for them is a great punishment﴾, i.e., they have returned with the wrath and anger of Allah, and for them in the Hereafter is a great punishment. The Exalted gave the reason for this great recompense in His saying: ﴿That is because they preferred the worldly life over the Hereafter﴾, through their disbelief in Allah and their not believing in Him, because of what that involves of freedom from worship, so there is no obedience, no lawful and no unlawful. And His Exalted saying: ﴿And that Allah does not guide the disbelieving people﴾ is a threat from Him, the Exalted, whose knowledge preceded it, that the disbelieving people are deprived of the grant of guidance as a punishment for them for choosing disbelief and persisting in it.

And His Exalted saying: ﴿Those are the ones upon whose hearts Allah has set a seal﴾, and upon their hearing and their sight. Those whom Allah threatened with not being guided are those upon whose hearts a seal has been set, so they do not understand; ﴿and their hearing﴾, so they do not hear admonitions nor the call of the callers to Allah, the Exalted; ﴿and their sight﴾, so they do not see the signs and proofs of Allah in the universe. Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 16, verses 103–109:

Explanation of the words:

Bashar (a human being): they mean a Christian smith (blacksmith) in Makkah.

Lisan alladhi yulhiduna ilayhi (the tongue of the one they incline towards): i.e., they incline towards it.

Wa hadha lisanun 'arabiyyun (and this is a clear Arabic tongue): i.e., the Qur'an, so how could a non-Arab (a'jami) teach it?

Illa man ukriha (except one who is compelled): i.e., compelled to utter disbelief, and he uttered it.

Wa lakin man shara bil-kufri sadran (but whoever opens his breast to disbelief): i.e., he opened his breast to disbelief and expanded it for it, so that his soul was content with it.

Wa ulaika hum al-ghafilun (and those are the heedless): i.e., heedless of what is intended for them.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 16, verses 110–113:

Explanation of the words:

Hajaru: that is, to Madinah.

Min ba'di ma futinu: that is, the polytheists of Makkah tested them and tortured them until they uttered the word of disbelief under compulsion.

Inna Rabbaka min ba'diha: that is, after the emigration (hijrah), the striving (jihad), and the patience upon faith and jihad.

La-Ghafurun Rahim: that is, Forgiving toward them and Merciful toward them.

Yawma ta'ti: that is, remember, O Muhammad, the day when every soul comes pleading for itself.

Mathalan qaryah: it is Makkah.

Rizquha raghadan: that is, abundantly.

Fa-kafarat bi-an'um Allah: that is, with the Messenger, the Qur'an, security, and the abundance of living.

Fa-adhaqaha Allah libasa al-ju': that is, due to a drought that befell them, so that they ate the hair-like fibres (al-'ihn) for seven years.

Wa al-khawf: since the military expeditions (sarayat) of Islam came to raid them and cut off their trade routes.

Meaning of the verses:

After Allah, exalted is He, mentioned the concession of uttering the word of disbelief under compulsion, on condition that the heart is not at ease with disbelief, He mentioned, informing about some of the believers who lagged behind in emigrating after the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. When they wished to emigrate, Quraysh prevented them and tortured them until they uttered the word of disbelief. Then they were enabled to emigrate, so they emigrated, strove, and were patient. Allah, exalted is He, informed about them that He grants them His forgiveness and mercy, so they will not fear nor grieve. Allah, exalted is He, said: ﴿Then indeed your Lord﴾, O Messenger, ﴿toward those who emigrated after they were tested﴾, that is, were tortured, ﴿then struggled and were patient – indeed your Lord, after that, is Forgiving and Merciful﴾, that is, Forgiving toward them and Merciful toward them.

And His saying, exalted is He: ﴿The day every soul will come pleading for itself﴾, that is, remember that, admonishing the believers with it, meaning, [every soul] will argue seeking salvation for itself. ﴿And every soul will be paid in full for what it did﴾, that is, of good or evil. ﴿And they will not be wronged﴾, because Allah is Just; injustice is impermissible in His judgment, and He does not wrong.

And His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And Allah presents an example: a city that was secure and tranquil﴾, that is, Makkah, ﴿safe from the raids of enemies, tranquil, not visited by fear or dread, because of what Allah placed in the hearts of the Arabs of reverence for the Sacred Precinct and its inhabitants; ﴿its provision comes to it abundantly﴾, that is, in plenty, ﴿from every place﴾, as it comes to it from Syria and Yemen during their two journeys in summer and winter. ﴿But it denied the favors of Allah﴾, which is its denial of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, its rejection of monotheism, its persistence in polytheism, and its waging war against Islam. ﴿So Allah made it taste the garment of hunger﴾: the Messenger prayed against them, "O Allah, make them [suffer] years like the seven hard years of Joseph," so drought struck them for seven years, and they went hungry until they ate carrion and the hair-like fibres. And He made it taste the garment of fear, as the military expeditions of Islam began to intercept their trade and even raided them in the heart of their homes. And His saying, ﴿for what they used to do﴾, that is, Allah requited them with hunger and fear because of their corrupt conduct, which was the persecution of the believers after their disbelief, polytheism, and persistence in that. And His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And there had certainly come to them a Messenger from among themselves﴾, he is Muhammad ﷺ, ﴿but they denied him﴾, that is, they rejected his message, denied his prophethood, and waged war against his call; ﴿so the punishment seized them﴾, the punishment of hunger and fear, while they were ﴿wrongdoers﴾, that is, polytheists and wrongers of themselves, since by their disbelief they exposed themselves to the punishment of hunger and fear.

Guidance of the verses:

From the guidance of the verses:

1- The virtue of emigration, striving, and patience, and that these acts expiate sins and erase transgressions.

2- The obligation to remind of the Last Day and of the reward and punishment that take place therein, so as to turn away from this world and turn toward the Hereafter.

3- The commendability of giving examples by the people of knowledge.

4- The disavowal of blessings through their loss and the retribution upon their people.

5- Denying the Messenger ﷺ in what he brought, even by turning away from it and not acting upon it, brings calamity and punishment.

**Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on Surah 16, Verses 114–118**

**Explanation of the words:**

*Fakulu* (so eat): i.e., O people.

*Halalan tayyiban* (lawful and good): i.e., not forbidden and not repugnant.

*Wa-ishkuru ni'mata Allahi 'alaykum* (and be thankful for the favour of God upon you): i.e., by worshipping Him and by refraining from what He has forbidden you, turning instead to what He has made lawful for you.

*In kuntum iyyahu ta'buduna* (if it is indeed Him you worship): i.e., if you worship Him alone, then comply with His command: eat of what He has made lawful for you, and leave what He has forbidden you.

*Al-maytatu* (carrion): i.e., any animal that has died by its own accord without proper ritual slaughter (*tadhkiyah*).

*Wa-al-dam* (and blood): i.e., flowing blood that is poured forth, not blood mixed into flesh or bone.

*Wa-ma uhilla li-ghayri Allah bihi* (and that over which the name of other than God has been invoked): i.e., that over which a name other than the name of God the Exalted has been pronounced.

*Ghayra baghin wa-la 'adin* (neither desiring it nor exceeding the limit): i.e., not transgressing against anyone, nor exceeding the limit of necessity.

*Wa-la taqulu lima tasifu alsinatukumu al-kadhiba* (and do not say, concerning what your tongues describe falsely): i.e., do not declare things lawful or unlawful with your tongues, lying against God, saying "this is lawful and this is unlawful" without any lawful or unlawful ruling from God the Exalted.

*Wa-'ala alladhina hadu* (and upon those who were Jews): i.e., the Jews.

*Harramna ma qasasna 'alayka min qabl* (We prohibited what We have already related to you before): i.e., in Surah al-An'am.

**Meaning of the verses:**

God the Mighty and Majestic bestowed His favour upon His servants. He permitted them to eat of the lawful and good provision He had granted them, and to thank Him for it by worshipping Him alone. This is the attitude of one who worships God alone: he thanks Him for the blessings He has bestowed upon him.

As for His words, ﴿He has only forbidden you carrion, blood, the flesh of swine, and that over which other than God has been invoked﴾, they mean: do not forbid what has not been forbidden to you, such as the *sa'ibah* (animals released freely), the *bahirah* (a she-camel slit-eared and released), and the *wasilah* (a ewe or she-goat that produced female twins), which the polytheists forbade as fabrication and lying against God.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 16, verses 119–124:

Explanation of the words:

﴿Then indeed your Lord, for those who did evil in ignorance⦆: that is, then indeed your Lord is Forgiving and Merciful to those who did evil in ignorance and then repented.

"after that": that is, after the ignorance and the repentance.

"Indeed, Abraham was a nation": that is, an imam (leader) comprehensive of all the qualities of good, a model to be emulated in that.

"devoutly obedient to Allah, upright (ḥanīf)": that is, obedient to Allah, inclining toward the upright religion, which is Islam.

"He chose him": that is, his Lord chose him as a khalīl (intimate friend) after the message and prophethood.

"And We gave him in this world good": it is the good praise from all the people of the heavenly religions.

"The Sabbath was only made for those who differed concerning it": the Jews were commanded to honor Friday, but they refused and insisted on the Sabbath, so Allah imposed it upon them and made it stricter for them as a punishment.

Meaning of the verses:

After the verses had, over a long context, condemned polytheism and the denial of resurrection and prophethood by the disbelieving, obstinate polytheists, and the surah's context was nearing its end, Allah the Exalted opened the door of repentance for them and said: ﴿Then indeed your Lord﴾, that is, with forgiveness and mercy, ﴿for those who did evil in ignorance﴾, who associated others with Allah, denied His revelation and denied the meeting with Him, ﴿and then repented after that﴾, who affirmed His oneness by worshipping Him, acknowledged the prophethood of His Messenger, believed in the meeting with Him and prepared for it with righteous deeds, ﴿and reformed﴾ what they had corrupted in their hearts, deeds and states, ﴿indeed your Lord after it﴾, after this repentance and sincere return, ﴿is Forgiving and Merciful﴾ toward them. So this was glad tidings for them through the tongue of the Book of their Lord.

His saying, the Exalted: ﴿Indeed, Abraham was a nation, devoutly obedient to Allah, upright, and he was not of those who associate others with Allah, grateful for His favors. He chose him and guided him to a straight path. And We gave him in this world good, and indeed he, in the Hereafter, is among the righteous. Then We revealed to you: follow the religion of Abraham, upright, and he was not of those who associate others with Allah﴾. Since among the claims of the polytheists was that they were upon the religion of their father Abraham, builder of the House and establisher of the rites and sanctifier of the Sacred Precinct, and the Jews and Christians likewise claim to be upon the religion of Abraham, all of them insisted that they follow the religion of Abraham, and they rejected Islam on the pretext that what they were upon was the religion of Allah which Abraham, father of the prophets, peace be upon him, brought. And as a means of nullifying falsehood, removing the veil of doubts and purifying the truth for the call of truth and the true religion, Allah the Exalted mentioned a portion of Abraham's spiritual and religious life as a living, speaking example for every sensible person: when he looks at it, he knows whether he is one who follows Abraham and lives upon his religion or is other than that. Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Indeed, Abraham was a nation﴾, that is, a righteous imam comprehensive of the qualities of good, whom every person desiring good emulates. This is first. Second, he was devoutly obedient, that is, obedient to his Lord, disobeying Him in no command or prohibition. This is Abraham. Who, then, has the greater claim to be associated with him? The polytheists? No! The Jews? No! The Christians? No! The monotheistic Muslims? Yes, yes! O Allah, make us among them, gather us in their company, and honor us on the day You honor them.

And His saying, the Exalted: ﴿The Sabbath was only made for those who differed concerning it﴾. In it is evidence refuting the claim of the Jews that they are upon the religion of Abraham and his great religion, since honoring the Sabbath was not part of the religion of Abraham. Its cause was that Allah the Exalted revealed to one of their prophets that he should command the Children of Israel to honor Friday, but they differed about that and preferred the Sabbath out of obstinacy and arrogance, so Allah prescribed for them the honoring of the Sabbath. His saying ﴿Indeed your Lord will judge between them on the Day of Resurrection concerning that in which they differed﴾ contains a warning to them that He will repay them with evil for their rebellion against their prophets and their opposition to them.

Guidance from the verses:

1- The door of repentance is open to every sinner, whether the sin is great or small, on condition of sincere repentance: immediate cessation, remorse, constant seeking of forgiveness, and reforming what has been corrupted.

2- Affirmation of tawhid and proclamation of the status of Abraham, peace be upon him, explanation of his perfections and Allah's favor upon him.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 16, verses 125–128:

Explanation of the words:

*ila sabili rabbika* (to the way of your Lord): that is, to His obedience, since obedience to God leads to His pleasure and bounty, so it is the way of God.

*bil-hikmah* (with wisdom): that is, with the Qur'an and with sound, firm speech that carries proof clarifying the truth.

*wal-mau'izhah al-hasanah* (and fair admonition): these are the admonitions of the Qur'an, and gentle, good speech.

*wa-jadilhum billati hiya ahsan* (and argue with them in the best manner): that is, with the debate that is better than any other.

*lahuwa khayrun lis-sabirin* (it is better for those who are patient): that is, better than retaliation in its outcome.

*wa-la taku fi dayqin mimma yamkurun* (do not be distressed by what they plot): that is, do not concern yourself with their scheming, and do not let your chest be constricted by it.

*ma'a alladhina ittaqaw* (with those who have taqwa): that is, who guard against shirk and sins.

*wa-alladhina hum muhsinun* (and those who are doers of good): that is, in obedience to God; His being with them (ma'iyyah) is His help and support for them in this world.

Meaning of the verses:

The Lord, exalted is He, addresses His Messenger, honouring him and assigning him a duty: *"Invite to the way of your Lord"* (ud'u ila sabili rabbika), that is, to His religion, which is Islam, all people. Let your invitation be *"with wisdom"* (bil-hikmah), which is the wise Noble Qur'an, *"and fair admonition"* (wal-mau'izhah al-hasanah), which is the admonitions, stories, parables, encouragement and warning of the Qur'an. *"And argue with them in the best manner"* (wa-jadilhum billati hiya ahsan): that is, dispute with them in the manner that is best, which is free of abuse, insult and innuendo of evil, for that is more likely to make the opponent accept the truth and what it calls to. His saying, exalted is He, *"Indeed your Lord knows best who has strayed from His way"* (inna rabbaka huwa a'lamu bi-man dalla 'an sabilihi) among people, *"and He knows best who are guided"* (wa-huwa a'lamu bil-muhtadin). He will recompense the one who is guided with his guidance and the one who is astray with his straying, just as He knows best who has gone astray and who has been guided from eternity. So make light of it for yourself, and do not overdo your invitation so that you harm yourself; the matter is not in your hands, but in your Lord's, who guides whom He wills and leads astray whom He wills. Your duty is only to invite in the manner described to you: with wisdom and fair admonition, and argue in the best manner. His saying, exalted is He, *"And if you retaliate, then retaliate with the like of what you were made to suffer"* (wa-in 'aqabtum fa-'aqibu bi-mithli ma 'uqibtum bihi), no more. *"But if you are patient"* (wa-la-in sabartum) and leave off retaliation, *"that is indeed"* (lahuwa), that is, your patience, *"better"* (khayrun) for you than retaliating for the sin and the offence. His saying, exalted is He: *"And be patient"* (wa-ut-bir), concerning abandoning what you, O Messenger, had resolved upon of mutilating the polytheists in retaliation for their mutilation of your uncle Hamzah. So He commanded him to be patient, and this entails abandoning both retaliation and mutilation together. His saying: *"And your patience is not except through God"* (wa-ma sabruka illa billah), that is, only through His enabling and help. So be with your Lord, seeking from Him patience just as you seek from Him help and victory. His saying, exalted is He: *"And do not grieve over them"* (wa-la tahzan 'alayhim), that is, over their failure to be guided to the truth, to take hold of it and to walk its path, which is Islam. *"And do not be in distress"* (wa-la taku fi dayq), of soul, which would pain you, *"because of what they plot"* (mimma yamkurun) against you, for God, exalted is He, is sufficient for you against their plotting and their evil; indeed He is with you, so do not fear and do not grieve, for He is with those who have taqwa and those who are doers of good, and you are among them. His saying: *"Indeed God is with those who have taqwa and those who are doers of good"* (inna Allaha ma'a alladhina ittaqaw wa-alladhina hum muhsinun): He, mighty and majestic, informs His Messenger and the believers that He, by His victory, support, help and enabling, is with those who guard against shirk and sins, who have not abandoned the obligations of their religion and have not violated its prohibitions, and with those who are doers of good in obedience to their Lord, sincere in intention and purpose, and performing acts in the manner that God has legislated and the Messenger of God ﷺ has explained.

Guidance from the verses:

1- The obligation of inviting to God, exalted is He, that is, to Islam, which is a collective obligation (wajib kifa'i): if a group undertakes it, it suffices for the rest.

2- An explanation of the method of invitation: it should be through the Book and the Sunnah, free of violence, harshness and severity, and debate should be in the best manner rather than otherwise.

3- It is permissible to retaliate by taking an amount equal to what was taken from a person, but leaving it off in patience and seeking reward is better.

4- God's being with those who have taqwa and ihsan is established, and it is a being of victory, support and guidance.
